#116. Donnie Wahlberg's Plane Skids Off Vegas Runway in “Intense” Incident

Donnie Wahlberg shared he’s OK after his plane skidded off the runway at a Las Vegas airport: “I'm just going to tell you these pilots saved our lives.”

Donnie Wahlberg is recounting a terrifying incident.

The New Kids on the Block member shared how he’s doing after the private jet he was on skidded off the runway at a Las Vegas airport.

“It was me and my team/friends onboard the aircraft,” Wahlberg wrote on Instagram Oct. 18 alongside a video of him detailing the ordeal. “It was a rather intense few moments (which felt like a few long minutes).”

“Thankful to God, of course, and to our incredible pilots who did an amazing job of keeping us safe and avoiding a serious disaster,” he added. “The airplane did take some lumps—but we did not. Thank you to all the emergency personnel on the ground in Las Vegas! You all were absolutely wonderful.”

Following the ordeal, Wahlberg—dad to sons Xavier, 33, and Elijah, 25, with ex-wife Kimberly Fey as well as stepdad to wife Jenny McCarthy’s son Evan, 24, from a previous relationship—shared he had sent the video to his loved ones to let them know he was safe.

But after “getting a lot of concerned messages and texts” about the failed takeoff—which occurred at Harry Reid International Airport, according to People—he decided to share the clip detailing what went awry publicly.

“We were taking off and didn't get up in the air and ran out of runway and the runway is way over there,” he explained in the video while pointing into the distance. “I'm just going to tell you these pilots saved our lives, and God covered us.”

“I'm not sure how many fences we avoided, but we didn't avoid the last one,” he continued. “But we avoided those trucks and heavy equipment and the dumpsters behind that.”

And while the Boston Blue actor gave the flight crew their flowers for getting him and his team to safety, he’s also crediting his faith for the near-fatal accident’s outcome.

“God is good,” he said in the video. “We just finished praying, and I looked out the window and said, 'We are not getting up in the air today, but we're safe and thankful, and all is well.'”

He continued, “Praise God. Thank you, Jesus.”

Keep reading for more stars who lived through freak accidents…

Jamie Lynn Spears' then-8-year-old daughter Maddie Aldridge was driving an ATV in February 2017 when she accidentally flipped it into a pond near their Louisiana home, leaving her submerged under water for minutes.

"When we were finally able to get her out of the water and I saw her and then the first responders took her from me, we thought she was gone," Jamie Lynn recalled on a 2020 episode of Maria Menounos Better Together podcast. "We thought we'd lost our daughter."

Though the family wasn't sure what sort of damage had been done, Maddie was awake and talking two days later. A few weeks after that, she was back to her normal routine.

"God gave me the blessing of giving me my daughter back," Jamie Lynn continued. "I lost her and I got her back."

Filming on Rebel Wilson and Anna Camp's 2025 action comedy Bride Hard turned dramatic during the Aussie's final day of playing secret agent. "In a fight scene, a gun accidentally got whacked across my face," Rebel explained to Access Hollywood in a June 2025 interview. "It was just a freak accident, and my nose got split open, so I left set. It was my last night of shooting. I was like, 'How unlucky can I be?'"

Surrounded by a pool of her own blood, "I was freaking out," she admitted of the 2023 incident. "They take an ambulance and they have to call a plastic surgeon, because if they didn’t, I would have been permanently disfigured. So we got the plastic surgeon, they did all the stitches, and you can’t tell now."

Tonight Show host Jimmy Fallon almost lost his finger after he tripped and fell in his own home. He tried catching himself on the counter and his ring got stuck on the way down, pulling his finger out.

He described it as "ring avulsion," and it kept him in the hospital for 10 days as doctors worked to prevent him from having to get it amputated.

An experienced hiker who competes in distance running, swimming and triathlons, Zane Wach was nearly felled by altitude sickness while hiking with his dad Ryan Wach on California's Mount Whitney in June 2025.

"He started to experience some hallucinations," Ryan explained to to the SFGATE of the 14-year-old. "He knew he was hallucinating. He said he saw things like snowmen and Kermit the Frog."

Ryan managed to stop his teen from walking off the cliff multiple times as they made their way back down the trail. “He was in an altered mental state, and I don’t know what caused it. We still don’t know,” the father noted. “My best guess is a combination of exhaustion, sleep deprivation, probably some dehydration and lasting effects from the altitude sickness. But he essentially started to doubt reality.”

And on a third attempt, Ryan was too far away to catch Zane, watching as his son fell roughly 120 feet off the cliff. After waiting six hours for an Inyo County Search & Rescue helicopter to get there and fly Zane to Southern Inyo Hospital in Lone Pine, he was stabilized and transferred to a pediatric trauma center in Las Vegas. Placed into a medically induced coma, he eventually began breathing on his own.

“It’s going to be a survival story in the end," Ryan said of his teen, who suffered head trauma along with a broken finger, ankle and fractured pelvis, "but right now we’re still in the middle of it."

On New Years' Day 2023, Avengers star Jeremy Renner was using a snowplow to tow a truck that was stuck in the snow on the driveway of his Lake Tahoe home. But after exiting the machine, he was pulled under while trying to stop the plow from hitting his nephew and suffered 38 broken bones.

"As I lay on the ice, my heart rate slowed, and right there, on that New Year’s Day, unknown to my daughter, my sisters, my friends, my father, my mother, I just got tired," he wrote in his 2025 memoir My Next Breath. "After about thirty minutes on the ice of breathing manually for so long, an effort akin to doing ten or twenty push-­ups per minute for half an hour . . . that’s when I died."

Fighting broken bones, blood loss and the threat of hypothermia, "I know I died—in fact, I’m sure of it," he wrote. “When the EMTs arrived, they noted that my heart rate had bottomed out at 18, and at 18 beats per minute, you’re basically dead."

TikToker Emilie Kiser and her husband Brady Kiser were forced to face the unimaginable when their 3-year-old son Trigg Kiser fell into the pool at their Arizona home in May 2025.

Chandler Police Department told USA Today that officers responded to a drowning call at a residence on May 12, for a child who had been pulled unconscious out of a backyard pool. Both police and firefighters administered CPR on the scene, before taking Trigg to Chandler Regional Hospital. But, sadly, the toddler died six days later.

Emilie later filed a lawsuit against Maricopa County public offices requesting that the court prohibit the public release of details surrounding his death. "Emilie is trying her best to be there for her surviving son, two-month-old Theodore," the lawsuit stated. "But every day is a battle."

A family vacation to Thailand turned into "the worst 10 days" of Dr. Cara Hodgson's life after she was electrocuted by power lines in December 2023. After blacking out and being rushed to the ER, the influencer spent the next week and a half "going in and out of hospitals fighting to regain my strength and fighting for my life," she detailed in a New Year's Day Instagram post. "I am so lucky to be here today."

As such, the orthodonist found a new reason to smile through the pain. The experience "taught me something I think we all need to be reminded of when we get caught up in the little things: What a precious privilege it is to be alive," Cara shared, "being able to breathe, eat, talk, move your body, is something grand and something to be celebrated."

Tragedy occured when Brazilian tourist Juliana Marins was hiking on Mount Rinjani, an active volcano in Indonesia, in June 2025. After she fell off a cliff (but not into the volcano's crater), a team of 48 search and rescuers spent four days "hindered by adverse weather, terrain and visibility conditions in the region," the Brazilian government shared in a statement, and eventually located Juliana's body.

"Today, the rescue team managed to reach the place where Juliana Marins was,” detailed a post on an Instagram account providing updates from her family. “With great sadness, we inform you that she did not survive. We remain very grateful for all the prayers, messages of affection and support that we have received."

When former Beverly Hills, 90210 star Tori Spelling attended a 2015 Easter brunch at Japanese restaurant Benihana, she tripped and burned her right arm on one of the Hibachi grills. After undergoing skin grafts to treat the injury, the actress ultimately deciding to sue the restaurant.

“I have a skin graft that they had to take from my leg," she later detailed on a 2024 episode of her and Jennie Garth's podcast 9021OMG. "Not many people can say, 'Hey, I'm wearing my thigh on my arm,' and I'm not even kidding. So I'm wearing a thin layer of my thigh on my arm because the skin burnt so bad."

When comedian Tony Knight attended France's Rock&Cars festival in June 2024, he was killed after two large branches fell from a tree. "He was only 54 and having the time of his life," Joanne Allen, the sister of Tony's longtime partner Hayley Wright detailed in a GoFundMe message. "He was fit, healthy, happy and had everything going for him. He was charismatic, funny, passionate."

And, of course, adored by his longtime love. "He was an exceptionally talented man, with so many strings to his bow," Haley wrote in her own Instagram post. "There really was nothing he couldn’t do. He was a fantastic friend to so many, an amazing dog Dad….but most of all he was my world & it will never be the same without him."

A company celebration turned catastrophic in January 2024. To kickoff the planned 25th anniversary festivities for Chicago-based software company Vistex, CEO Sanjay Shah and president Vishwanath Raju Datla were suspended in an iron cage meant to be lowered 20 feet onto a dais at the India-based party, a company official told The Times of India. Instead, two wires snapped, causing the men to crash onto the concrete stage.

Sanjay, 56, died of his injuries at the hospital following the accident, the paper reported, while 52-year-old Vishwanath sustained a severe head injury and passed months later.

"When I was 19 I fell three floors from a window and broke my back," Orlando Bloom shared in a joint 2022 Instagram video with UNICEF. He had been trying to climb to the rooftop terrace of a three-story building with friends when the drainpipe he was scaling collapsed. Though he broke several vertebrae in his back, "I was very fortunate to survive the fall because my spinal cord was still just intact."

Still, he detailed, "When I was in the hospital, I was told for the first four days that I may never walk again. That was really the beginning of what was a long and painful journey for me into recognizing and understanding some of the patterns that had been in my life that had led me to having numerous accidents. And the culmination was breaking my back, which was a near-death experience."

Leaving the hospital in a back brace with heaps of physical and emotional pain, "I started partying straight away—with the back brace on," he shared with GQ in 2005. "It took me a couple of months to realize this was my life, and I didn't want to mess it up."

The experience has "informed everything in my life," he added. "Until you're close to losing it, you don't realize. I used to ride motorbikes and drive cars like everything was a racetrack; it was ridiculous. It wasn't because I thought it was cool; it was just because I loved living on the edge. But I've chilled."

#117. Sean Connery's Cult '70s Sci-Fi Movie Is The Perfect Goofy Watch On Prime Video

John Boorman was already difficult to pin down before he directed "Zardoz." By then, he'd made "Catch Us If You Can" (the Dick Clark Five's shot at matching The Beatles' "Can't Buy Me Love"), the avant-garde noir "Point Blank," the intense (if creatively compromised) World War II drama "Hell in the Pacific," and the bizarre morality play "Leo the Last." Everything changed when he landed a primo studio assignment with "Deliverance," which earned him Oscar nominations for Best Picture and Best Director. In the early 1970s, Boorman was a hot New Hollywood property, but he had the loftiest of ambitions.

After "Deliverance," Boorman wanted to adapt J.R.R. Tolkien's "The Lord of the Rings," but United Artists, which, less than a decade later would kneecap itself by backing Michael Cimino's Western "Heaven's Gate," got cold feet. So, since he couldn't tackle Tolkien, Boorman decided to create an original fantastical universe set in the distant future and addressing adult, dystopian themes. He dreamed big, although it wound up being too big for his "Deliverance" backer Warner Bros. So, his agent David Begelman, who later developed a bad habit of endorsing checks written to Cliff Robertson, got him a meeting with 20th Century Fox.

His idea, "Zardoz," is a richly imagined tale set in the year 2293, where society has splintered into a haves/have nots dispute between Eternals and Brutals. The latter are immortal with multiple caveats (life gets boring when you can't die), while the Brutals are encouraged to kill each other by a floating stone head (Zardoz) that exhorts "The gun is good, the penis is evil." Fox greenlit this absurdity on a $1.5 million budget, and Boorman got Sean Connery to star. The result was one of the greatest cult movies ever made, and it's currently streaming on Prime Video.

I was around 10 years old in 1983 when I fell asleep in front of the television while watching "Saturday Night Live" and woke up to a late, late night broadcast of "Zardoz." I couldn't figure out why Sean Connery (who made the movie to escape his James Bond legacy) was running around in a red, bandolier-equipped onesie complemented by knee-high leather boots, but I did know I was watching something special. Once I established I wasn't dreaming, I locked into one of the weirdest films I'd ever seen.

Since I'm writing this for people who've never seen "Zardoz," I'm not going to spoil the mind-blowing reveal. Just know that John Boorman whips the carpet out at a certain point, which causes a massive reframing of everything you've been watching. It's fascinating to watch Connery vacillate from Brutal to a more enlightened being, and he strikes up some zesty chemistry with Charlotte Rampling's Consuella (an Eternal). Dramatically, the film lags at times. Boorman takes pains to explain the minute details of what it means to live forever, and the concept is intriguing. It's like a slow-going rendition of Stephen King's yet-to-be-adapted short story "The Jaunt." It's longer than you think, and, at a certain point, catatonia seems like a pretty sweet deal.

"Zardoz" isn't a movie you'll want to revisit often, but it's one you'll want to kick over in your head for the rest of your life. It's classic Boorman. He didn't make it to get the next greenlight. He made it because he couldn't leave it festering in his brain.

#118. Marshals' [Spoiler] Undergoes Chemotherapy After Several Character Deaths

Yellowstone‘s spinoff Marshals explored a main character’s cancer diagnosis by having them undergo chemotherapy.

During the Sunday, October 18, episode of the show, Cal (Logan Marshall-Green) was preparing for his first appointment after telling the squad about his health scare. He urged everyone not to come with him but Cal subsequently struggled emotionally when alone at the hospital.

Luckily, Belle (Arielle Kebbel) showed up to support her boss — and love interest. The episode ended with Cal smiling as Belle joined him amid his ongoing personal challenges.Cal was originally diagnosed in season 1 and is the show’s second character to battle cancer — following Kayce’s (Luke Grimes) late wife, Monica (Kelsey Asbille).

Yellowstone, which aired from 2018 to 2024, introduced Us to Kayce and Monica, who remained at the center of the show until the finale.

After teaching at a local school on the Broken Rock Indian Reservation, Monica went on to become a professor at Montana State University while navigating life with Kayce, who moved them back to the Yellowstone Ranch following his past tension with dad John (Kevin Costner).

Following John’s death, Kayce, a former U.S. Navy SEAL, became the new owner and operator of the Yellowstone Ranch. Kayce and Monica ended the show alive — and were still together — before Marshals began.

When the series premiered in March, however, fans learned Monica had died after battling cancer.

“Kayce had such a perfect ending in Yellowstone,” showrunner Spencer Hudnut told TVLine at the time. “His dreams had finally come true. As we were trying to figure out how to tell the next chapter in Kayce’s story, it felt like he really needed to be shaken out of that. Unfortunately, tragedy tends to find Kayce, so something bad was going to happen for him one way or the other. It just sort of played out that it was going to be Monica.”

Hudnut said Monica’s death will continue to drive Kayce, adding, “To me, Monica is really guiding Kayce through this first episode, trying to help him find his new path. And if you actually break it down, Tate is at that rally to honor his mother, and Kayce goes there to protect Tate. So if not for Monica, Kayce never would have been in that position and may not have found this path.”

He concluded, “We really wanted to be respectful of the way that we said goodbye to her. I also didn’t want to step on the ending of Yellowstone, because what they had was a beautiful ending. Unfortunately, real life intervened.”

Asbille, 35, has not yet broken her silence on Monica’s onscreen death. She did grant access for her likeness to be used on the show, which allowed Marshals to include photos of the fictional character on screen.

Marshals airs on CBS Sundays at 8 p.m. ET before streaming the next day on Paramount+.

#120. 2027 Oscars Best Actress Predictions: Winner, Runner-Up And Other Contenders

After people got to see Jessie Buckley's extraordinarily powerful performance as a grieving mother in Chloé Zhao's acclaimed literary adaptation "Hamnet," a handful of folks, including me, declared that she was the obvious frontrunner to win the Academy Award for Best Actress at the Oscars. That turned out to be completely true, and Buckley ended up sweeping pretty much every major precursor before taking home Oscar gold in the spring of 2026. Following in the footsteps of luminaries like Michelle Yeoh, Emma Stone, Olivia Colman, Frances McDormand, Meryl Streep, and Helen Mirren is no easy feat, but in the spring of 2027, one performer will rise to the top of the pack and take home the next Oscar for Best Actress.

So, who's in the running? We can't know for sure, but I'm here to make some semi-educated guesses about who could win, who could pull an upset, and who could end up snagging one of the five nomination spots in the first place. Aside from our projected winner and projected "runner-up" (the one who could pull the aforementioned upset), everyone is listed in alphabetical order. With that out of the way, let's look at who has the best shot at pulling out a victory at the 2027 Academy Awards for their excellent 2026 role.

Hear me out: What does the Academy love more than an ingénue? Brie Larson, Jennifer Lawrence, and Mikey Madison all won Oscars for high-profile roles relatively early in their careers, which means that breakout "Obsession" star Inde Navarrette could have a straightforward path to Oscar gold. If you're not familiar with Navarrette, I have to ask: Where have you been? Alongside Michael Johnston (who plays Baron "Bear" Bailey), Navarrette headlined Curry Barker's surprise 2025 horror hit "Obsession," an extraordinarily dark parable of sorts that begins when Bear uses a strange artifact to wish that Navarrette's Nikki loved him more than anything in the world. True to the film's title, Nikki is suddenly devoted to Bear, but her lack of agency invites truly unsettling questions, and Barker uses his relatively simple conceit to interrogate consent, love, and, well, obsession.

Again, Navarrette is a fresh-faced star who's now set to appear in Marvel Studios' X-Men movie reboot, and the Academy loves that sort of thing. (To bring it back to Lawrence for a moment, she was midway through her own franchise, the "Hunger Games" movies, when she won for "Silver Linings Playbook" in 2013.) In addition, Amy Madigan pulled out a somewhat surprising but wholly deserved win early in 2026 for her supporting turn as the witchy Aunt Gladys in "Weapons," confirming that, despite years of bias, the Academy is coming around on the horror genre. (I'm still pretty ticked off that Lupita Nyong'o, just a few short years after winning in the Best Supporting Actress statue for "12 Years a Slave," didn't even get nominated for her dual performance in Jordan Peele's "Us" due to the organization's clear anti-horror stance.) Add in Michael B. Jordan's victory earlier for another horror movie in "Sinners," and you've got the right environment for Navarrette to win.

Julianne Moore didn't win her first Academy Award until 2015 for her role as a woman grappling with Alzheimer's disease in "Still Alice," and while I personally preferred Rosamund Pike's unbelievable turn as Amy Elliott Dunne in "Gone Girl" that same year, I couldn't ever argue with Moore taking home an Oscar after four previous nominations (for "Boogie Nights," "The End of the Affair," "Far from Heaven," and "The Hours"). Moore has been an exciting and audacious performer for decades, and she hasn't earned an Oscar nomination, period, since winning for "Still Alice." I think her role in Jesse Eisenberg's second film as a director, "The Debut," could change that.

In this sharp, funny flick, Moore stars as Mona Friedman, an introverted New Jersey housewife who finds herself thrust into the spotlight when she books the lead role in a local theater production spearheaded by the notoriously tough director Jerry Blankenbuehler (Paul Giamatti, who also feels like a likely pick for an Oscar nomination, only in the Best Supporting Actor category). Alongside incredible co-stars like Bernadette Peters, Lilli Cooper, Halle Bailey, Bonnie Milligan, and Eisenberg himself, Moore shines as Mona and completely vanishes into this unexpectedly tricky role, leaning into the movie's wildest moments with complete ease. The bottom line is, never, ever, ever rule out a red-haired performer who takes on an audacious, attention-grabbing role, even if she's a relatively recently-crowned Oscar winner. Remember when Emma Stone won for "Poor Things" mere years after her first victory for "La La Land?"

I don't think Emily Blunt will win an Oscar for her lead role in Steven Spielberg's ambitious summer blockbuster "Disclosure Day," but I do think that she'll end up snagging a nomination for this attention-grabbing role. Blunt stars in the film as Margaret Fairchild, a Kansas City meteorologist whose broadcast is interrupted one day when she starts speaking in odd clicks and noises before passing out. When she regains consciousness, Margaret suddenly possesses psychic abilities and, eventually, links up with whistleblower Daniel Kellner (Josh O'Connor), learning that the two have been connected for years ... and that the United States government has been working with shadowy organizations to hide the existence of aliens from the general populace.

Blunt only earned her first Oscar nomination in 2024 for her work in Christopher Nolan's historic 2023 epic "Oppenheimer" (there, she plays Kitty Oppenheimer, the troubled wife to Cillian Murphy's titular physicist), and even if your mileage varies when it comes to "Disclosure Day" as a whole, Blunt's performance is undeniably fantastic. Despite Margaret's increasingly bizarre circumstances and understandably emotional reactions to a series of wild reveals, Blunt imbues the character with a steely resolve that makes her feel entirely human. Basically, I think that between her performance and the fact that we're talking about a Spielberg original, Blunt will probably make it into the Best Actress category.

Because Sandra Hüller's astonishing 2023 run — where she appeared in a lead role in "Anatomy of a Fall" and a supporting one in "The Zone of Interest" — predated the Academy's recent rule changes (per Variety) that permit performers to earn separate nominations in different categories, she's only been nominated for one Academy Award for the former, even though she deserved it for both. (Hüller is incredible in "Anatomy of a Fall," but her turn as the wife of a high-ranking Third Reich official in "The Zone of Interest" is haunting, terrifying, and astounding, too.) Now, once again, Hüller finds herself in a situation where she could very well pick up multiple nods, and voters will also have to make some tough choices. I can't fully rule out that Hüller will break into the Supporting Actress category for her turn in the beloved blockbuster "Project Hail Mary," but when it comes to the Best Actress race, she actually has two viable pathways: "Fatherland" and "Rose."

If I'm being blunt, Hüller could easily earn a Best Actress nomination for "Rose," Markus Schleinzer's 17th century period drama that casts her as a soldier (the titular Rose) who lives as a man in a small Austrian Protestant village. I'm going with "Fatherland," though. It's directed by Paweł Pawlikowski and has Hüller portraying real-life figure Erika Mann, the daughter of the acclaimed novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler). I don't think there's any question that, at some point in her career, Hüller will accept an Oscar in front of a cheering crowd, and "Fatherland" might get her in the running for 2027.

In a just and fair world, the way that Olivia Wilde's Angela says "jamón" in "The Invite" would have her swimming in a pool of Oscars, Scrooge McDuck-style. Wilde, who followed up her 2022 critical dud "Don't Worry Darling" with "The Invite" and handily proved she's still one of our most exciting working directors despite that misfire, stars in this claustrophobic, weird, and wildly funny movie that only features her, Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz, and Edward Norton as two couples at the world's most out-of-control dinner party. After Joe and Angela (Rogen and Wilde) decide to invite their neighbors Hawk and Pina (Norton and Cruz) over for dinner, things quickly spiral out of control — partly because Angela and Joe are so wildly unhappy in their marriage, and partly because of lingering resentment on their part that they can always hear Hawk and Pina during, uh, intimate moments.

My jaw dropped multiple times during the run of "The Invite," and every single performer here is doing great work, but Wilde is on another level. Her frantic, twitchy, bug-eyed Angela has outsized reactions to nearly everything, as if she can't help herself, and despite sounding hyperbolic, I'm being accurate and correct when I say that some of Wilde's on-screen reactions are making new innovations in facial movement. If Wilde manages to earn a spot in both the Best Director and Best Actress Oscar categories (which, in my opinion, she should), that would be history-making for the Academy — and even though I think her winning Best Actress is sort of a long shot, I'd love to see her nominated.

We'll find out who's nominated for an Oscar on January 21, 2027, when said nominees are announced. The ceremony will then take place on March 14.

#121. Selena Gomez Discusses Nicotine Addiction, Reveals It's Altered Her Voice

Selena Gomez has opened up about her nicotine addiction, revealing that vaping has permanently changed her voice.

“I’m not going to be able to change my voice. I vaped nicotine a lot and just so everyone knows, that’s somewhat … vaped,” Gomez, 34, said in a candid Sunday, October 18, Instagram Story video, using a hopeful past tense to describe her habit. “Nicotine is so hard to quit and I think I just wanted to say, if you’re going through it or even if you’re trying to vape, it’s just not worth it.”

The Only Murders in the Building star, who has been photographed several times with a vape in her hand over the years, continued, “It’s so stupid and it’s changed my voice so if you guys don’t like listening to my voice, that’s totally understandable. I don’t mind, just don’t listen. But I am really excited, because I stopped and I just hope I can keep it up. It’s really hard, but I know if you are going through something, you can get through it too. It sucks.”

Gomez has vaped for quite some time, revealing the apparatus in her hand as she got ready to marry husband Benny Blanco and also seemingly holding the pen while preparing for an outing with Taylor Swift last year. In August 2018, she was snapped clutching a vape while walking in Rome, Italy.

Her public address comes after months of scrutiny over subtle changes to her voice over the years, and it isn’t the first time she’s addressed concerns shared online. In December 2025, the actress acknowledged during an Instagram Live session that fans had flagged apparent vocal changes.

“There’s no excuse, I don’t really care,” she said during her December 16 Instagram Live session. “I think my point is that sometimes things happen. I get weird [or] my throat swells from the inside sometimes. That’s all.”

She added at the time that she welcomed such frank conversation. “I’m glad y’all are being real with me on the Live. I appreciate it though, for real,” she said.

More recently, Gomez also opened up about how as she gets older, physical traits are bound to change. During an interview with People on September 16, she said that aging doesn’t frighten her.

“I don’t feel like it’s a bad thing,” she explained. “Getting older has been so fun. I’m not scared at all. I love getting older. Things are going to change and things are going to sag, but you’re alive. I think age is just a number in many ways.”

After Gomez’s nicotine admission went live, she followed the clip with a cute mirror selfie while wearing a pair of tortoise shell spectacles, indicating that things were business as usual. Additional Instagram Stories that followed included a fresh-faced outdoor selfie that captured her glowing skin, as well as fan videos that praised her beauty brand, Rare Beauty.

Love Island USA’s Melanie Moreno revealed to E! News at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show where she and Sincere Rhea stand today.

Melanie Moreno and Sincere Rhea are keeping it chill.

After the pair received heat not just from the Fijian sun, but also from the audience over their journey on Love Island USA, Melanie and Sincere are moving forward at their own pace.

News at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show Oct. 18. “I know people want to see us post and they want to see us, but we've only known each other in the villa for so little time. Because while their romance may have started under unusual circumstances—a.k.a. while filming a reality series on a tropical island—Melanie emphasized she and Sincere are normal people.

You get real people behavior, and I'm happy. And even if me and him decide to date or we don't decide to date, he's a really good friend of mine. He's also been a person that has helped me while I'm living this new life.”

And while she and Sincere take “the normal route” towards a full-fledged relationship, Melanie emphasized the good vibes she and all her loved ones are feeling.

"I’m really taken care of,” she said. “I pinky promise you—my mommy's happy, my sister's happy. We're all happy. Like genuinely, I feel so supported in my life right now, and just like I feel really good right now, so that's all I have to say with that. Take it as you will, but I feel really good, and I think that's what I feel like my supporters would want is for me to feel good.”

Melanie’s update on where she and Sincere, 25, stand is not a big departure from what the pair shared during the Love Island USA season eight reunion in August.

At the time, the two emphasized they were not an official couple.

"We are not boyfriend and girlfriend," Melanie said during the cast sit down. "We are kind of just seeing what happens in the outside world. I think he’s building that trust. I think we’re building it. We’re seeing how it goes."

As for Sincere, he, too, pointed to the unusual circumstances in which their love first ignited.

"We’re on the same exact page as far as, you know, being—it’s not like we met each other at a bar," he said. "Being able to just take it slow and really get to understand each other outside of here."

In the meantime, Melanie is enjoying life out and about following the end of her time on Love Island, stunning in a gorgeous black dress at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion show. For more from the night’s pink carpet, read on.

#123. Why M. Bison From Street Fighter (2026) Looks So Familiar

The main antagonist of the "Street Fighter" series is M. Bison, crime boss of the Shadaloo organization, who dresses like a military dictator. In "Street Fighter" video games and animation, numerous voice actors have played Bison, from Canadian actor Richard Newman ("Beast Wars") in the West to Norio Wakamoto ("Dragon Ball Z," "Cowboy Bebop") in "Street Fighter" parent company Capcom's native Japan.

M. Bison has also been brought to live action in three "Street Fighter" films. The late Raul Julia (best known as Gomez Addams in the 1990s "Addams Family" films) played Bison in the 1994 "Street Fighter" film. In fact, it was Julia's last film role before his death, and he's widely considered the best part of the movie. Neal McDonough played the villain in 2009's "Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li," though without the character's famous outfit. In the new 2026 "Street Fighter" film (which includes a tribute to Julia), Bison is played by David Dastmalchian, an actor skilled at both comedy and playing genuinely disturbed villains.

Dastmalchian's film debut was in "The Dark Knight." He had a brief but memorable role as Thomas Schiff, one of the Joker's henchmen, who gets interrogated at gunpoint by District Attorney Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart) — an early sign of Dent's two-faced dark side. Since then, Dastmalchian has appeared in many other DC Comics productions (and he's discussed his habit of playing comic book characters with /Film).

He appeared as Polka-Dot Man in "The Suicide Squad," with small guest roles on TV series "Gotham" and "The Flash." Dastmalchian also appeared as Kurt, one of Scott Lang's (Paul Rudd) criminal friends, in the Marvel movies "Ant-Man" and "Ant-Man and the Wasp."

Dastmalchian has also contributed to DC Comics animation; he voiced the Penguin and Calendar Man in the animated film "Batman: The Long Halloween," Mr. Freeze in the H.P. Lovecraft-inspired "Batman: The Doom That Came to Gotham," and most recently played the Riddler in "Batman: Knightfall."

With how many superhero movies and TV David Dastmalchian has been in, it's not surprising he even has a side career as a comic book writer. But his career is far more varied than just geek media.

In 2023, Dastmalchian worked with "The Dark Knight" director Christopher Nolan again on "Oppenheimer." He had a small but crucial role as William Borden, director of the Joint Committee on Atomic Energy and the author of the pivotal, slanderous letter to the FBI accusing J. Robert Oppenheimer (Cillian Murphy) of being a Soviet double agent. He also had a small role in the first "Dune" film as Piter De Vries, a Mentat employed by the Harkonnens.

In the 2024 horror film "Late Night with the Devil," Dastmalchian got a chance to lead a movie. "Late Night with the Devil" is presented as unearthed footage from the 1970s showing a genuine demonic possession, and resulting murders, on a talk show. Dastmalchian plays the program's host, Jack Delroy, who may or may not have struck his own deal with the Devil.

Outside of films, Dastmalchian has a prolific TV career, too. His most recent roles include Gurathin in the Apple TV sci-fi series "Murderbot," and Mr. 3 in Netflix's live-action adaptation of legendary manga "One Piece." Now, he can add M. Bison to his long list of roles.

As the 2026 TV schedule pushes on, Grey’s Anatomy is entering its 23rd season, meaning fans are getting reacquainted with their favorite doctors at Grey Sloan Memorial. Of course, the season has already kicked off with an intense trauma, steamy romance and surprising twists, but through all of this, I still have one question. With Grey’s officially back, where does the upcoming spinoff stand? I’ve been looking for an update, and someone finally asked the executive producer.

ABC announced in May that it had ordered a Texas-based offshoot of Grey’s Anatomy. This marks the third spinoff of the long-running medical drama, following Private Practice and Station 19. The news definitely came as a surprise to me, and the series set to premiere during midseason 2027. It’s set in rural West Texas at a medical center, but not many details have been released, including a premiere date or a title. Grey’s showrunner Meg Marinis, who co-created the spinoff with Shonda Rhimes, recently shared an update with The Hollywood Reporter that will make fans happy:

We are working away. I can’t say much, but we’re far enough along where I’m really, really excited. We’re digging into the actual communities and true stories of what happens out in rural West Texas. There’s so much going on there that I haven’t seen on TV. I’m thrilled to be able to dive into that world. It’s so different from Grey’s. It’s related to Grey’s, but its stories are going to be different.

Considering how many medical dramas are currently on TV and how prevalent they've been over the years, I was skeptical at first. But, since it seems like the new series will be tackling subject matter that other medical shows have not, and throwing that against the backdrop of rural West Texas, I’m definitely intrigued. I’m even more eager to how this show is going to be connected to Grey’s Anatomy and how it will also differ from its parent show.

Considering Grey’s has had two successful spinoffs in Private Practice and Station 19, which ran for six seasons and seven seasons, respectively, I wonder if this show might have similar longevity. With three successful shows in the Grey’s franchise at this point, it's fair to wonder if the creative team feels pressure to keep the momentum going. But, when it comes to making the new spinoff, there's a special element for Marinis that goes beyond lessons learned from previous shows:

The only lessons are good lessons from those two. They were very successful spinoffs with hardcore fan followings. I loved both of them. This one is something dear to my heart [Marinis is from Houston, Texas] and being on a medical show like Grey’s, and hearing a lot about what’s happening in medical deserts, it’s hard to show that in Seattle. I’ve always been really interested in showing it, and in doing a small town show in Texas.

Since this is a spinoff and there are connections to Grey’s Anatomy, many people, like myself, have been wondering just how the new series will debut. While Marinis couldn’t give any proper updates since things are still being worked on, she did make sure to note that both shows are getting the proper attention they deserve:

We have thoughts based on airing schedule and things like that, but we’re still working it out, also because there are so many things going on on Grey’s, I want to make sure to do it where it’s servicing both shows equally.

As of now, it’s unknown how many episodes Grey’s Anatomy will be getting this season, but there have been reports that the drama could be getting a shorter season to make room for the spinoff. With the 9-1-1 franchise taking up two-thirds of ABC’s Thursday slot and possibly airing full seasons, there’s no telling what things will look like in the new year. What is clear is that the Grey’s franchise is not going anywhere any time soon, and I'm hopeful about what's to come with the spinoff.

In the meantime, though, new episodes of Grey’s Anatomy air on Thursdays at 10 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day with a Hulu subscription.

#126. Deathstroke's Canceled DCEU Movie Storylines Explained By Joe Manganiello

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Joe Manganiello has revealed the unrealized plans for his Deathstroke, aka Slade Wilson, in the DC Extended Universe. Often referred to as the Snyderverse, the DCEU came before James Gunn and Peter Safran took over as the heads of DC Studios. Ben Affleck wanted Deathstroke for his canceled "Batman" film, but that didn't pan out. However, as Manganiello has now explained, many other ideas were on the table.

Manganiello's only screen time as the Deathstroke character came during credits scenes attached to "Justice League," but plans had already been hatched for more. During an interview with Rich Roll to promote his memoir "Bloodlines," Manganiello revealed that the brass at Warner Bros. had more than a few notions about how to utilize him as Deathstroke. That, at one time, included a "Deathstroke" movie from "The Raid" director Gareth Evans, which also didn't pan out. Still, the studio did at least consider him for other projects on the way. Per Manganiello:

"I got to play the character again for, like, two minutes in the reshoots. And for the next six years, there were just project after project and call for my agent after call for my agent about, 'Oh yeah, they're going to use your character in this. You're going to be in this. You're going to be the villain in 'Aquaman 2.' You're going to be in 'Suicide Squad 2' with this director. No, this director. No, you versus Will Smith. Oh, it's going to be a standalone.' Am I lucky or unlucky?"

The "Suicide Squad" sequel lost Will Smith as Deadshot due to scheduling conflicts. Evidently, WB wanted to make a Deadshot vs. Deathstroke movie of some kind after that as well. But that didn't happen, nor was Deathstroke included in "Aquaman 2," which became "Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom."

We got our first official look at Joe Manganiello as Deathstroke in November 2017, i.e. damn near nine years ago. Once Ben Affleck's "The Batman" was canceled, though, it was clear that Warner Bros. still wanted to use the actor in some capacity. But the DCEU didn't have a clear direction, as evidenced by the many proposed projects that Manganiello listed off.

"I'm lucky that I got that part, but at the time, I felt like I was unlucky because I got this thing that then got canceled and went away," Manganiello added. "So, I'm like, how unlucky am I? I feel like I'm cursed. I get this thing. It gives me hope, and now it's gone. And then all these other projects are now gone. But looking back, I was lucky that that thing came my way."

Manganiello had serious health issues, resulting in a surgery where his entire large intestine was removed. Hence, as he explained, getting in shape for his DCEU role may well have helped save his life:

"If it wasn't for that role, I don't know that the reconnection would work. I don't know that I'm healthy enough. I don't know that I gain that weight back. I don't know that I can walk. I don't know that I can function the way that I do now. I don't know that mentally I'm in as good a place as I am now. That role. I have the helmet in my office, and it's the greatest accomplishment of my life."

Presently, DC Studios is developing a "Batman" villain team-up movie featuring Bane and Deathstroke for the DC Universe. Unfortunately, Manganiello isn't expected to be involved.

You can order Joe Manganiello's "Bloodlines" from Amazon.

#127. Jasmine Tookes Reacts to Heavy Wings at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show

Model Jasmine Tookes slammed the "awful" claim that she was "fighting for her life" during the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show because of her weight of her angel wings.

Heavy are the shoulders that wear the wings.

Jasmine Tookes cleared the air after a viral clip showed her declaring that the wings she wore during the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show were "so heavy."

"Oh my god lol," she commented under a video of the moment shared to Instagram Oct. 18 that claimed she was "fighting for her life" on the runway. "This is awful..you caught me on the way back when i was almost off the stage…"

Tookes added, "Gave it my all going to the camera if you watch the real show."

Indeed, the model stunned on the runway in a multicolored bikini look that featured a sequined magenta cover-up over her bottom half that was paired with giant, tinsel-covered pink angel wings.

Tookes—who appeared a second time during the show in an all-white lingerie look worn under a beaded cover-up—shared how content she was with how the night went.

"You guys I'm so happy!!!" she posted to her Instagram Stories Oct. 18. "I will share so many fun moments tomorrow. Time for some champagne. LOVE YOU ALL."

While Tookes was joined on the runway with many fellow longtime Victoria's Secret models like Gigi Hadid, Adriana Lima, Alessandra Ambrosio and Candice Swanepoel, there was at least one veteran of the show that skipped out this year: Miranda Kerr.

Two decades after she made her debut at the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, Kerr revealed why she didn't hit the catwalk this year—despite being invited to return.

"Looking back with so much gratitude for the friendships, the magical memories and for everyone who made that chapter of my life so special," Kerr—who last walked in 2012—captioned her Sept. 17 Instagram post. "It meant so much to be invited to return this year, especially as it marks 20 years since my first show."

"But I ultimately felt in my heart it was right to cherish this chapter as it was," she concluded. "Sending so much love and light to everyone in this year's show!"

Three years after David Gordon Green’s Exorcist: Believer didn’t hit well with critics, the storied horror franchise is getting a reboot with Mike Flanagan directing the installment. At this point, the fan-favorite filmmaker has earned a great reputation for effectively telling haunting stories, and I’m confident he’ll be the perfect man for the job. With Flanagan providing his own terrifying take on one of the best horror movie franchises, he's apparently going without a key aspect of the series, and he has a good reason for it.

What makes the original Exorcist so intense even for seasoned fans, other than Regan’s gruesome possession, is its chilling score. But, when Flanagan spoke to ComicBook, he revealed that the infamous "Tubular Bells" wouldn't be featured in The Exorcist: Martyrs. That wasn't a decision Flanagan made lightly, though:

That was something I was pretty adamant about (not including). It felt at that point that we were surrendering some of our unique identity in favor of trying to pull that… For me, ‘Tubular Bells’ just kind of exists in amber in the Friedkin film. And it didn’t feel right to reach for it.

While “Tubular Bells” is a signature tune in William Friedkin’s 1973 masterpiece, I understand Flanagan’s stance on not wanting it to be in his 2027 movie release. It’s clear he wants to provide his own vision to a long-standing horror franchise. So, since he's not using the piano piece featured in Friedkin’s movie, I'm wondering if the Carrie director has something even more eerie in store. Considering he's working with frequent collaborators the Newton Brothers, I'd imagine the group will deliver something spine-tingling.

Still, Mike Oldfield’s “Tubular Bells” is certainly a haunting piece of work. It comes off in the beginning like a childlike lullaby that appears innocent, only for the melody to keep rapidly picking up the pace. Surprisingly enough, Oldfield’s track didn't even gain true prominence until it appeared in Friedkin's renowned horror film.

As for the reboot, another change that the Gerald’s Game filmmaker plans to make for his upcoming horror film is the scare factor. As he explained to Comicbook, modern audiences aren’t as freaked out as viewers were in the '70s when they first saw the movie. This is all the more reason why Flanagan is taking on the challenge of making Martyrs the “scariest movie” he’s ever done. And how will he do this? By showing that no Higher Power will “catch you” when the Devil makes an appearance. I’m already getting chills here.

So, while “Tubular Bells” will be sitting out Mike Flanagan's movie, it feels like there's still going to be a lot to look forward to. Flanagan's always been one to take creative swings, and I'm eager to see what he does with this flick. Get prepared for demonic possessions and religious strife when The Exorcist: Martyrs opens in theaters on March 12, 2027.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#130. This Late '40s Western TV Series Features An Actor We Don't Talk About Today

After John Ford pulled a legendary performance out of John Wayne in 1939's "Stagecoach," the once flailing genre was revitalized. Suddenly the Western moved out of "poverty row" and was taken seriously again. One man who straddled both sides of this seminal evolution of the genre was William Boyd, who in the 1930s and '40s played cowboy hero Hopalong Cassidy on the silver screen before bringing him to TV in yet another seminal moment for the Western. And yet you probably never heard of him.

Boyd's career stretched beyond his Western films. He started out as an extra in Cecil B. DeMille's 1920 comedy "Why Change Your Wife?" before re-teaming with DeMille for 1925's "The Road to Yesterday." This film proved to be his breakout role, and along with 1926's "The Volga Boatman" helped propel him to leading man status, allowing him to appear in some of the best films of the silent era. But by the early 1930s, having lost his contract, Boyd was struggling to maintain his standing. Soon, however, he'd land the role which revitalized his career and with which he became synonymous.

Hopalong Cassidy was a character created by writer Clarence E. Mulford. Cassidy walked with a limp due to an old gunshot wound, hence his nickname, and first appeared in the book "Bar-20" in 1906. This original incarnation of the character was much rougher and hard-bitten than the version Boyd came to define on-screen. Ultimately, the actor made the character entirely his own across an incredible 66 films produced between 1935 and 1948. Then, he brought Cassidy to the small screen, and by extension, introduced the Western to TV audiences.

Classic Western TV shows gave us such towering Old West heroes as Clint Eastwood's Rowdy Yates, James Drury's Virginian, and James Arness' Marshal Matt Dillon. But all of these icons of the small screen Western came in the wake of William Boyd's Hopalong Cassidy.

The actor first portrayed Cassidy in the 1935 film "Hop-Along Cassidy." But this was not the tobacco-chewing foul mouthed anti-hero of Clarence E. Mulford's stories. Boyd's version was upstanding in every way. Across 65 subsequent movies, his version of Cassidy traversed the frontier on his white horse, Topper, delivering justice in as morally upright a way as possible. That meant no drinking (he consumed nonalcoholic sarsaparilla), smoking, or drawing first in a gunfight. Boyd's Cassidy always preferred to bring outlaws in rather than shooting them down, and unlike Mulford's original character, never allowed himself profanity. He was the epitome of the white hat-wearing Western hero (though, strangely, he wore a black hat), and the character became inseparable from Boyd himself.

After 66 "Hoppies," as the films came to be known, Boyd decided it was time to bring Cassidy to the small screen. In truth, the film series was — as you might expect given the sheer volume of entries — running out of steam. But Boyd, who had made the last 12 Cassidy movies without the help of his longtime producer Harry Sherman, was determined to keep his version of the character alive, and bought the TV rights from original author Mulford. According to a Time article from 1950, the actor sold his ranch, mortgaged his car, and even moved into a bungalow in order to afford the $350,000 he needed for the TV rights and control of the Hopalong Cassidy films. It paid off.

In 1949, "The Hopalong Cassidy Show" debuted on NBC as the first Western TV series. Naturally, William Boyd starred as the title character, in a show specifically designed to appeal to younger audiences. When the show first started airing, it was nothing more than Hopalong Cassidy films re-edited for broadcast. But episodes filmed specifically for the show soon started to arrive, introducing Edgar Buchanan's Red Connors, a sidekick for Cassidy who was similarly taken from the pages of Clarence E. Mulford's stories.

The show was hugely popular, running from 1949 to 1952 and becoming a phenomenon among younger viewers, leading to lucrative merchandising deals. As the 1950 Time article put it, "Among all the U.S. enterprisers who devote themselves to titillating the unripened mind, none has succeeded as Hoppy has, both with his under-age customers and the thousands of manufacturers, retailers, and advertising men who hawk his wares." Suddenly, Hoppy merchandise was everywhere, and Boyd — who just a few years earlier had gambled everything on the Hopalong Cassidy TV rights — was a very rich man.

After the show ended and Cassidy faded from popularity, so too did Boyd disappear into obscurity. Western die-hards know his name today, but he's hardly as well known as other Western icons of both film and TV. Sadly, despite arguably being one of the most influential Western actors of all time, he seems to have struggled with the legacy of the character he made a household name. According to the Los Angeles Times, the actor hardly talked to the press prior to his death in 1972, at one point saying, "I'm not the man people remember as Hopalong Cassidy. I don't want to tamper with their memories."

#131. ‘I Look Like An A--hole’: How Jason Momoa Really Feels About Fans Asking For Photos In Public

Jason Momoa’s level of fame just seems to keep on growing. The A-lister has three major titles on the 2026 movie schedule alone -- Supergirl, Street Fighter, and Dune: Part Three -- are a true testament to just how sought-out he is at this point. So, considering Momoa's notoriety, how does he feel about people coming up to him in public and asking for photos? Well, the star provided some very honest thoughts on that.

Given Momoa's most badass roles, those pulsing tattoos, long, wavy hair, and muscles, it would be hard for the Hawaiian native to navigate the world incognito. On one hand, this status is pretty impressive for someone who started in Hollywood via a TV supporting role in Baywatch. But, on the other hand, while on Delightful Drinks, the Game of Thrones alum talked about how he draws a line when it comes to fans asking for his time outside of press duties:

It's tough for me. …. ‘Cause generally, people just get really really excited, and that's awesome ‘cause I get excited when I see people that I really like. But, if I'm out, like oh my god, I'm with someone I haven’t seen forever, or with my kids right now, I know people just don’t give a shit. I don’t get to see my kids that much. If you pull my attention away from something, I’m like, ‘I’m sorry. This is not the right time.’

The Stargate Atlantis actor isn’t wrong for wanting privacy when it’s most needed, like when spending time with his loved ones. After all, celebrities are humans, too. Momoa has indeed dealt wth the struggles of fame, like when he was being followed by the paparazzi in Italy back in 2022. While the Hells Angels crowd were there to help thwart them, I don’t think the motorcycle club whenever he's in public.

Constant requests for photo ops must not make the life of a celebrity very easy. Momoa continued to talk about times at which fans interrupt his alone time with his “lady,” Adria Arjona, and how he looks like an a-hole due to his honest rebukes of them:

[People,] they get happy, and they don’t know what’s coming out and, most of the time, I look like an asshole…. I'm not giving away my time to my children or if sometimes I'm with my lady. It's crazy, ‘cause guys are the ones. I'll be with my lady [and a guy is] like, ‘Dude, I need a picture.’ I'm like, ‘Bro, I'm with my lady right now, if you don't get the fuck away from me.’ Dude, I literally have my arm around my lady [and] I’m like, ‘Go away.’ And they’re like [gestures as if taking a selfie] ‘I love you, man!’ I’m like, ‘Get away, bro! You’re gonna get me killed!’

In short, don’t mess with Jason Momoa and his “lady”. Honestly, I can imagine how frustrating it could be for a celebrity when a fan to asks for a photo even while they're with their significant other. Someone would think the admirers would have the self-awareness to understand the famous actor is preoccupied.

Other celebrities can relate to this, like Anthony Mackie, who was bothered by a fan at a restaurant for a photo (only to get puked on). Fellow Marvel star Tom Holland used to be aggressive with public fan requests until Zendaya dropped some words of wisdom on how to be more approachable.

While Momoa may think he looks like a jerk when pushing away fan photo requests, he acknowledged that there is no right or wrong on anyone’s part and that it “comes with the job.” Ultimately, it’s about fans and celebrities finding a balance between creating a sweet photo moment with an idol and establishing personal boundaries.

Be sure to catch Jason Momoa in Street Fighter, which is playing in theaters now and in Dune: Part Three, which opens on December 18th.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

“All my girls are going to be here," Harvey said. “I was literally texting them before I got here, and I was like, ‘Where are they at? Where are they? Are they coming?’ They're gonna be here soon. I'm so excited to meet with them. It's gonna be so crazy.”

And while romances that began on the Peacock series can be fleeting, friendships formed in Fiji are forever.

“The sisterhood is super strong,” she shared. “I love those girls. They're like my family.”

As for whether they’ll be cheering her on if she were to dominate the VS runway someday?

“We’re manifesting,” she continued “Manifestation, power of the tongue, I'm big on it.”

And when that day comes, she has just the secret to feeling confident in her angel wings.

“Just be authentically yourself,” she said. “Don't try to be like anyone else. Just remain yourself, and then that confidence is there.”

Dancing With the Stars’ Jenna Johnson and Harry Shum Jr. are ready to take on the ballroom for Dedication Night after discourse surrounding their lift last week.

In a Sunday, October 18, Instagram video, Shum Jr., 44, expertly lipsynced Glee’s rendition of “I Say a Little Prayer” as a nod to his past on the show. Johnson, 32, and Shum Jr.’s wife, Shelby Rabara, danced behind Shum Jr. and lip synced the backup vocals.

“So excited for dedication night 👯‍♀️✨ @shelbyrabara @harryshumjr #dwts #glee,” Johnson captioned the clip.

In a separate video uploaded to the official DWTS Instagram Story, Johnson shared that the duo are performing a foxtrot. As Shum Jr. appeared in the background, he began singing John Mayer’s “Stop This Train.”

“Such a good John Mayer song. And who are we dedicating it to?” Johnson said, as Shum Jr. shared, “Shelby. My wife.” Johnson added, “We are so excited.”

Days before, controversy began when Johnson and Shum Jr. performed a samba to Usher’s “Yeah!” featuring Lil Jon and Ludacris for Super Bowl Night — and judge Carrie Ann Inaba critiqued the routine for featuring an illegal lift.

“I think you need to put more content in your dances. Especially because [Harry’s] so good, I want to see you challenge yourself a little bit more in the vein of what we’re looking for. And there was a lift,” Inaba said, while Johnson appeared surprised and replied, “A lift?”

Inaba then read the definition of a lift from a piece of paper, adding, “A lift is — I just need to say it — any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner. Yeah, lift.”

Johnson and Shum Jr. were ultimately safe from elimination after receiving a combined score of 33 out of 40 from Inaba, Derek Hough, Bruno Tonioli and guest judge Joe Buck.

After the episode aired, Johnson’s husband and fellow DWTS pro, Val Chmerkovskiy, stoked drama when he defended his wife on social media. In a since-deleted TikTok, Chmerkovskiy appeared to reference Will Smith infamously slapping Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars and telling the comedian to “keep my wife’s name out your f***ing mouth.”

“You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” Chmerkovskiy wrote, a reference to Smith’s iconic Fresh Prince of Bel-Air role.

Inaba, for her part, took to Instagram to respond to the comment, writing, “So this is what we are doing now?”

News broke on Saturday, October 17, that Chmerkovskiy would not make an appearance on Dedication Night. Instead, his season 35 partner, Jenna Dewan, would perform a Viennese waltz with pro Alan Bersten. Chmerkovskiy issued a statement on his post on Saturday.

“In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife, I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention,” Chmerkovskiy wrote in a statement shared with Us. “Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was.”

He continued at the time, “The last thing I want is to become a distraction from an important week or from the incredible work my dance partner Jenna Dewan is putting in. Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole DWTS family lots of love during Dedication Night. I’ll be watching and cheering everyone on!!”

When Megan Fox first stepped into motherhood, she was also cultivating a growing career on screen. Between the time she welcomed her three sons with her now-ex-husband, Brian Austin Green, Fox was appearing in several projects, including starring as April O’Neil in the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles franchise and her recurring role as Reagan Lucas in New Girl, while Zooey Deschanel was ironically on maternity leave herself. With her fourth child, which she welcomed with ex-fiancé MGK, Fox took a different approach to being a working mother.

Unlike the first three times she gave birth, Fox was determined to spend valuable time with her daughter, whom she welcomed in March 2025. This meant stepping away from Hollywood and social media altogether. It was a move that was important to the Transformers actress, who has expressed regret over not being able to do the same for her sons. Fox shared her thoughts on motherhood with PEOPLE while promoting her campaign with Ro, saying:

Having to separate from my other kids early was always really painful. It affected my mental health, and it affected my physical health as well. Being able to really be present with her has been something that I love, and I’m so grateful that I got the chance to do it this way.

Even though Fox has been able to be present with her daughter Saga since her birth, the actress shared that she still felt guilty when she’d have to step away to answer phone calls or handle other household chores. "Mom guilt" is a common feeling that many mothers have to deal with in those early days of parenthood.

Nevertheless, the Midnight in the Switchgrass star simply seems grateful to have had the opportunity to work in a manner that's more conducive to her role as a mom. While reflecting on raising her first three kids as a younger actress, she recalled being "in a position where I had to work," and that was something she didn't feel good about at the time. It sounds like that's changed considerably with Saga Blade, though:

I’ve been able to choose to be much more present, and I have a lot more peace in my connection with her because of that.

Now that Saga is a year old, Fox has slowly begun to return to the spotlight. The star has been making headlines for her lingerie-inspired fashion choices and for selling her own “feral” soap. Most recently, Fox has also been taking her racy photos to Subs.com. However, this isn’t just a place for Fox to post exclusive content that won’t be available anywhere else; she’s also becoming the co-owner of the website along with Stokely.

In addition to those new endeavors, Fox also has at least one major acting gig on the horizon in the form of Jennifer’s Body 2, which she already seems to be channeling through her fashion choices. It's also rumored that the movie will begin filming sometime this month in Vancouver, though that's far from confirmed. What is known for sure is that the sequel is being penned by OG writer Diablo Cody and is slated to have Fox and Amanda Seyfried return to their roles.

Unfortunately, Jennifer’s Body 2 won’t be finished in time to make the 2026 movie schedule, but it’s definitely an upcoming horror movie to be excited for next year. And, as production arrives, let's hope Megan Fox is able to maintain the balance she's sought between work and motherhood.

#136. Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson Ejected for Spitting on Raiders' Brock Bowers

Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected and flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct after spitting on Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers on Sunday, October 18.

The bizarre incident happened late in the second quarter of the teams’ game at Las Vegas’ Allegiant Stadium, as the two players were jawing with one another after a play.

CBS Sports cameras picked up the spit flying out of Gardner-Johnson’s mouth, which earned harsh criticism from legendary play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz.

“This is about as disrespectful as it gets,” Nantz, 67, said.

Rules analyst Gene Steratore was brought in for commentary, calling the act “something we just don’t want to see in the game.”

The CBS Sports halftime panel had similar thoughts, with an impassioned Nate Burleson calling out Gardner-Johnson for the move.

“What are you doing?” Burleson, 45, questioned. “I get it, scuffles happen. Jaw jacking happens. But you can’t do this. One, it’s childish, it’s immature. And it’s unprofessional. You’re supposed to be one of the veterans on the team and you get kicked out of the game for spitting?”

C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct pic.twitter.com/S2ME5wNiRT

— NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026

Pro Football Hall of Fame coach Bill Cowher called Gardner-Johnson “selfish.”

“In games like this, your ability to control your emotions and stay focused will be the difference in this game,” Cowher, 69, added.

Gardner-Johnson signed a one-year, $6 million contract with the Bills in March.

The NFL veteran, who is currently playing with his sixth franchise, is no stranger to scandal — even when it comes to spitting.

During his time with the New Orleans Saints in 2020, Gardner-Johnson was accused of spitting on Chicago Bears wide receiver Javon Wims amid a scuffle between the players. Gardner-Johnson denied spitting on Wims, though he was ultimately fined $5,128 for his involvement in the fight.

After winning the Super Bowl as a member of the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025, Gardner-Johnson wore a sweatshirt that said “Swifties Can LIX My Balls” to the team’s victory parade. The Eagles had defeated Swift’s then-fiancé, Travis Kelce, and the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX.

“Should’ve Stayed with that thick s—’, Gardner-Johnson wrote via his Instagram Story shortly after the Super Bowl alongside a photo of him taunting Kelce, 37, during the game.

The post was seemingly a dig at Kelce’s relationship with his ex-girlfriend, Kayla Nicole, who the Chiefs star dated shortly before he began seeing Swift. Kelce and Swift, 36, got married in July.

The horror genre has been thriving for a while now, and 2026 has certainly been no exception. Both Backrooms and Obsessions crushed it simultaneously at the box office, and the latter has become a pop culture sensation. I mean, Freaky Nikki is even a character at Hollywood Horror Nights. I recently re-watched the movie for the first time with my Peacock subscription, and one line in particular hit me like a ton of bricks... pun intended.

Obsession's most gruesome scene happened in its third act, when Wish Nikki violently kills Sarah by smashing her head repeatedly into a brick until her face is basically demolished. I was gearing up to watch this scene again from the comfort of my home, and it turns out that one early line of dialogue totally set it up.

Fans have been wondering what happens to Nikki after Obsession's ending, where she's freed from the wish and surrounded by her friends' dead bodies. While we're not expecting a direct sequel, Curry Barker hinted that things probably didn't go well for Nikki. After all, there's a ton of evidence pointing to her being a murderer, especially after Sarah and that brick.

It turns out that moment was totally foreshadowed early into Obsession's 109-minute runtime. When Bear gives Nikki a ride home from the bar, she says that she's only able to talk really honestly with him. She speaks about how he's a good listener at work, saying:

My jaw pretty much hit the floor when I heard this line. Obviously, it went in one ear and out the other when I saw Obsession in the movie theater, but Curry Barker's script was subtly hinting at what would be Wish Nikki's most violent act. It makes me appreciate how specific the filmmaker's vision for the movie was, and further shows why he is deserving of all the flowers coming his way.

Given Obsession's wild critical and box office success, all eyes are on what Curry Baker will bring to the horror genre next. Many people are hoping for a direct sequel to the film, while Nikki actress Inde Navarette would like to see the filmmaker do an Obsession anthology series. There are more One Wish Willows out there, and each of them can have a unique story about the dangers of wishing something into existence. We'll just have to see if we ever get a follow-up to the fan favorite movie, or if Barker pivots and brings something different altogether for his next project.

Obsession is streaming in all its glory on Peacock as part of the 2026 movie release list. If you haven't given the movie a second watch since seeing it on the big screen, I highly recommend it.

Tributes are still pouring in for late actor RJ Mitte, who famously played Breaking Bad character Walter White Jr. Mitte died by suicide at age 34 nearly a week ago, and he’s been praised for his work as an actor and for his efforts as an advocate for the disabled community. At the same time, rumors have also been swirling around Mitte’s career, with some sources alleging that by the time he died, he was in the midst of severe career and money struggles. Now, Mitte’s mother is seeking to provide clarity on those rumors.

Dyna Mitte has been speaking out about her son in the aftermath of his passing and, in the process, she’s been candid about the circumstances in different respects. After speaking out, Dyna explained that she was the person who found RJ’s body at his home in Texas. The Mitte matriarch also spoke to The Hollywood Reporter, during which mentioned the speculation swirling around her son’s acting career to “straighten that out.” Per Dyna, contrary to reports, RJ had a lot on his plate from a professional standpoint:

They used to say, ‘You may do a thousand auditions before you land one job.’ Well, obviously it doesn’t work that way today. Of course, COVID made things kind of slow but things picked back up. But honestly, R.J. had three movies that have already come out this year. He has two more coming out. He has already signed deals on several new movies that he was going to be filming. There were talks of different things. He had a book coming out. He had a food truck he was starting. He had a lot going on.

Shortly before his death, Mitte had actually been promoting one of his 2026 movie releases, Talking to Strangers. It was during that press tour that the late star not only discussed some of the biggest Breaking Bad moments but also talked about having experienced financial hurdles following the show’s conclusion in 2013. Mitte himself said his attempts to team his professional team together proved to be costly, though there’s also been a rumor about a manager allegedly absconding with much of his money. On that topic, Dyna said:

There had also been speculation about a financial situation involving a manager. That happened years ago, had already been resolved, and was not related to what happened now.

Mitte starred on all five seasons of Breaking Bad and appeared in several of its best episodes. After news of Mitte’s passing broke, former co-stars like Bryan Cranston, Anna Gunn and Aaron Paul paid tribute. Days before his death, the Triumph star also hung out with another BB alum, Luis Moncada. Per Moncada, Mitte was dealing with unspecified difficulties before his passing and had arranged a hot air balloon outing to help give him an outlet. Moncada also explained that he’d offered Mitte the chance to stay with him and his son.

Even now, Mitte remains well known for his role as Walt Jr., and many continue to discover his strong performance on Vince Gilligan’s iconic drug dealer drama. That’s still, however, just one portion of Mitte’s legacy, as he used his voice to speak up for those living with cerebral palsy like he did. And, for his acting and advocacy efforts, SAG-AFTRA honored him with the Harold Russell Award.

RJ Mitte was most recently honored this past Friday, October 16, during a Celebration of Life ceremony that took place at the Mitte Center in Brownsville, Texas. Dyna Mitte was moved by the event, which was attended by a considerable number of people. Aside from clearing the air on RJ’s career and finances, she also said that she was doing her best to navigate the situation and was “taking one step at a time.”

Kylie Jenner shared a behind-the-scenes look at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show on Instagram, including a close-up shot of the $50 million Fantasy Bra that she closed the show in.

Indeed, the Kardashians star gave fans an intimate behind-the-scenes look at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, which she closed with a surprise appearance wearing the $50 million Fantasy Bra.

The 29-year-old shared a photo of herself to her Instagram Stories Oct. 18 of herself backstage before getting into the diamond-encrusted garment, sporting a pink striped silk robe embroidered with her name on the lapel which she wore over a nude bra. In the sultry snap, she played with her hair while her bottom half is covered in a pink-and-white striped blanket.

In another shot, Kylie declared that it was the "BEST DAY EVER" over a close-up shot of the Fantasy Bra, which features a fringe of jewels hanging from the band surrounding a 75.54-carat $22 million diamond at the bra's center.

The Kylie Cosmetics founder—who was the first person to wear the bra since Elsa Hosk in 2018 and the first non-Victoria's Secret model to ever wear it—joined the likes of Gisele Bündchen, Heidi Klum, Tyra Banks, Adriana Lima, Alessandra Ambrosio and Candice Swanepoel as women who had been bestowed the honor of wearing the iconic piece.

At the event, mom Kris Jenner and boyfriend Timothée Chalamet were there to support her from the audience. In fact, Victoria's Secret’s official social media account shared another backstage moment of Kris telling her youngest daughter that she was "incredible" on the runway as she gave her a big hug.

After the show, the brand defended its decision to cast Kylie in the show to wear the Fantasy Bra.

“Kylie really extends beyond fashion, beyond culture, beyond TV, beyond one singular thing,” Victoria's Secret chief creative officer Adam Selman explained in a Vogue interview published Oct. 18. “That’s the exact same thing that we do. Like, the show is so big, it’s true entertainment, and I think that she is a great catalyst for that."

"She’s really created her own culture, which—how many people can say that?" he continued, explaining that the "big idea for the show was fandomonium."

"I think it’s an interesting pairing that we’re giving the fans: we’re giving them what they want with this amazing Fantasy Bra, and we’re going to put it on an unexpected talent who has a massive following and massive cultural impact," Selman added. "I think it’s fun. I think it’s really joyful, and I think it’s fun to celebrate in a different way that people aren’t going to expect."
