Domhnall Gleeson has had more than a few pinch-me moments throughout the course of his career, partially due to his tenure with the Star Wars movies. By playing the villainous General Hux in the Sequel Trilogy, Gleeson had the opportunity to take part in some big scenes with A-list actors. The experience wasn’t always easy, though, and that wasn’t necessarily due to production. Gleeson actually revealed that his angrier portrayal of Hux in 2017’s The Last Jedi was due to a gross situation he experienced off the set.

Upon his debut in 2015’s The Force Awakens, Hux was shown to be a tense individual and staunch supporter of the First Order. I thought he was uptight enough in that initial installment, but Gleeson ramped it up for the aforementioned sequel. My first guess would’ve been that the star found an acting method to reach that level of anger, yet I never would’ve guessed that it really had to do with bedbugs. While on The Drew Barrymore Show, Gleeson recalled the matter after being asked to share a BTS memory:

Bedbugs. I was staying in a hotel the night before my first day shooting, and I got eaten alive by bedbugs. And the hotel said that they didn’t have bedbugs and that I was imagining it and that was a lie. And then they suggested that I wear pajamas. That was the solution to not being bitten.

I can think of few things that would make someone uncomfortable like bedbugs would, and the Paper star’s situation just sounds miserable. While he may have had a miserable first day on the Harry Potter set due to an accent mixup, I don’t think that compares to this critter-related situation. Still, Gleeson managed to turn lemons into lemonade, as he told Barrymore (as seen on YouTube) that he used the energy for his own benefit:

So, when I look at that, I just think I was probably really itchy that day. That’s why I look so angry, I think. That’s why I played it like that.

A part of me really wants to use my Disney+ subscription to watch The Last Jedi right now, considering this new information I’ve learned regarding those bedbugs. If anything, I applaud Gleeson for remaining professional even amid the less-than-deal circumstances. The film shoot wasn’t all bad for Gleeson either, as he even collaborated on a particularly fun (and dark) moment, which saw Hux aiming to finish off his boss, Kylo Ren, following a lightsaber battle.

How Rian Johnson Responded After Kathleen Kennedy Claimed He Was ‘Spooked’ By Negative Reactions To Star Wars: The Last Jedi

For the most part, Gleeson has spoken highly of his time within the Star Wars franchise. However, as was the case with this recent interview, he’s also been honest about the elements he wished were different. Gleeson previously admitted that he would’ve loved to have played a larger part in 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker. More recently, he also said he found Hux’s death in that film to be “devastating.” Yet, for Gleeson, what softened the blow of his character's demise was that it was the great Richard E. Grant – in character as Allegiant General Pryde – who delivers the fatal blaster shot.

I feel as though Star Wars fans have likely seen the last of Hux, though Domhnall Gleeson is down to return should an opportunity arise. For now, though, I’ll just settle for his insightful behind-the-scenes stories, and I really hope that any others he reveals aren’t as nasty as his bedbugs experience.

I can see the positives, but also a whole lot of negatives, in this prediction.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I like HBO because it still feels like one of the few places willing to spend serious money making television worth talking about. I have plenty of complaints about House of the Dragon, especially its pacing, but when one of those massive battles hits, and an enormous dragon screams out of the clouds, I can see where the budget went. Ben Affleck, however, has an idea about how we might get that spectacle faster. And it has me worried.

A clip of the Argo filmmaker discussing artificial intelligence, see below, has resurfaced in a post from Yashar Ali on X. The footage actually comes from a 2024 CNBC Delivering Alpha event, where Affleck was asked whether AI might threaten filmmaking. His answer was mostly optimistic about human creativity, but his example involving House of the Dragon and Succession has stuck with me for a much less cheerful reason:

Ben Affleck says the day will come when someone can order up an episode of Succession with a plot they have in mind. He says that could create an extra revenue stream to replace lost DVD revenue. Affleck says AI isn’t going to end the film and TV business, but certain parts of the industry will be dramatically affected: “I wouldn’t like to be in the visual effects business. They’re in trouble because what costs a lot of money is now gonna cost a lot less….And maybe it shouldn’t take a thousand people to render something.” But he says the cost savings will mean more television programming, not less: “You might be able to get two seasons of House of the Dragon in a year instead of one.”October 17, 2026

Affleck doesn't think AI overlords will take over all of cinema anytime soon. However, he suggests generative AI could take some of the expensive, time-consuming work out of effects-heavy TV. As he put it:

You might be able to get two seasons of House of the Dragon in a year instead of one.

That probably sounds fantastic to anyone who spent two years waiting for HotD to return on the 2026 TV schedule. Showrunner Ryan Condal has explained that filming alone can take roughly a year, followed by another seven months of making the dragons. I certainly wouldn't complain about shorter gaps between seasons if the resulting episodes were just as good.

Affleck then went further, imagining a day when someone could pay around $30 to request a custom Succession episode. Want Kendall Roy to win the company and run away with Stewy? Considering what actually happened in Succession's series finale, I can see why some viewers might be tempted to request a different ending. The Animals filmmaker acknowledged that the result might look awkward and argued that such uses should involve negotiated rights.

The Oscar winner also stressed that he did not expect AI to replace actual filmmakers. His broader argument was that cheaper production could mean more shows for viewers, which is a fair hope. Yet I'm less convinced studios will treat every dollar saved as permission to make better television.

HBO has earned its reputation with some of the most talked-about TV shows ever made, including The Sopranos, The Wire, Succession and Game of Thrones. Even when House of the Dragon frustrates me, the network still backs ambitious productions and lets talented people make difficult creative decisions. However, that doesn't mean the established auteurs won't still experiment with the tech.

High-profile filmmakers are already creating with the technology. Earlier this year, Darren Aronofsky's AI-generated American Revolution series raised similar concerns about the future of creative work. I mean, I personally wasn't a big fan of this piece of American history, considering it gave uncanny valley vibes. But, still, if Aronofsky is willing to throw his name behind AI, who's next?

Now, imagine an executive looking at AI-generated effects, shorter schedules and personalized episodes and deciding that viewers will accept a cheaper version of all that. The risk is that the technology becomes an excuse to squeeze budgets and crews while filling your HBO Max subscription with endless recognizable IP.

It's also worth remembering that House of the Dragon isn't delayed solely because someone needs to render scales on Vhagar. Actors have schedules. Scripts need revisions. Sets, costumes and whole performances have to come together. With that in mind, speeding up one part of the process does not magically solve everything else.

I understand why Ben Affleck sees opportunity here. I can even see AI tools helping artists with specific tasks. But the idea of ordering a disposable, computer-generated Succession episode leaves me cold. I want writers who know those characters deciding what happens to Kendall Roy, even when they make choices that drive me nuts.

HBO still sets a high bar for television. I'd rather wait for another great season than help teach the industry how far that bar can be lowered.

#144. Jenna Dewan, Alan Bersten Reunite Amid Val Chmerkovskiy’s Suspension

Val Chmerkovskiy’s celebrity partner Jenna Dewan and Alan Bersten shared an update on their Dedication Night performance amid Chmerkovskiy’s one-week Dancing With the Stars suspension.

Jenna Dewan and Alan Bersten are putting their best foot forward.

While Jenna’s partner Val Chmerkovskiy faces a one-week suspension from Dancing With the Stars, Dewan and Bersten shared an update on their rehearsals before they dance together during week six on Oct. 20.

“Hi everybody, it’s Dedication Night,” Dewan told cameras alongside Bersten in a video shared to the DWTS page’s Instagram Story Oct. 18. “And we are dancing a Viennese Waltz to ‘Unchained Melody’ by The Righteous Brothers, the greatest, most romantic song ever. So excited.”

The Step Up actress shared even more insight into her Dedication Night dance in an Instagram post, confirming she’d be dancing in tribute to her mom Nancy Lee Bursch.

“I’ve been thinking so much on all the things my mom has taught me throughout my life,” Dewan began the Oct. 18 carousel, which was full of photos with her mom over the years. “Not just in what she’s said, but in the way she’s lived and the example she’s always been for me.”

She continued, “To lead with kindness. To give people grace. To be strong without losing your softness. To keep your heart open, even when life doesn’t go quite the way you imagined.”

She wrote that her mom had long been her “biggest cheerleader” and was among the first to encourage Dewan in her dancing, which is why the Dedication Night performance feels so “full circle” for The Rookie actress.

“As life goes on, the more I realize that some of the greatest gifts our parents give us aren’t things at all,” she wrote. “They’re the values we carry, the love we pass on, and the way we choose to show up in this world.”

Dewan—mom to daughter Everly, 13, with ex-husband Channing Tatum as well as kids Callum, 6, and Rhiannon, 2, with fiancé Steve Kazee—continued, “And I hope more than anything that I make her proud! Not necessarily through what I do in life, but in the person I am and the way I move through life. Love you so much mom!! This one’s for you.”

As for Chmerkovskiy, the longtime pro was suspended from the competition series for one week after he alluded to Will Smith’s infamous Oscars moment in the wake of an awkward interaction between his wife Jenna Johnson and judge Carrie Ann Inaba.

But while some people interpreted his comments as a reference to Smith’s slap of Chris Rock, Chmerkovskiy was adamant he only meant to refer to Smith’s comment of, “Keep my wife’s name out your f--king mouth.”

“In a moment where my instinct was to defend my wife,” Chmerkovskiy wrote on social media following his suspension, “I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife's name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention.”

“Carrie Ann certainly didn't deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was,” he continued. “The last thing I want is to become a distraction from an important week or from the incredible work my dance partner Jenna Dewan is putting in.”

But in light of the news, he asked fans to show up with a little more during the special week.

“Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole DWTS family lots of love during Dedication Night,” he concluded. “I'll be watching and cheering everyone on!!”

Chris Hemsworth has spent more than a decade convincing audiences he could beat up just about anybody. Between playing Thor in the MCU and Tyler Rake in Netflix's Extraction movies, the Australian actor has built a career on looking like someone you would absolutely avoid upsetting in a bar. At 43, he apparently has no intention of slowing down. In fact, his latest workout footage has me impressed by how much time he's putting in for the third entry in the series.

While filming Extraction 3 overseas, Hemsworth shared an Instagram post showing off some seriously impressive striking drills with his friend and trainer, Jack Boonsanong. In the video below, the Avengers star can be seen working inside a boxing ring, throwing combinations, driving kicks into pads and generally looking like he could ruin my entire afternoon without breaking a sweat. And, considering the punishment Tyler Rake takes in these movies, I suppose that is exactly the point:

A post shared by Chris Hemsworth (@chrishemsworth)

In his caption, the Ghostbusters alum said he was shooting the third Extraction movie in Thailand and was fortunate to train with Boonsanong, whom he thanked for the session.

The footage is pretty remarkable. Viewers can see the Crime 101 star moving through punching combinations before switching to kicks and knees, with Boonsanong absorbing the blows on pads. The longtime Marvel staple looks comfortable doing it, which is slightly concerning when you remember this is supposed to be his day job between filming intense sequences for new action movies. I get tired carrying groceries into the house. This man apparently relaxes by throwing knees at people.

This isn't our first glimpse of Hemsworth preparing for the sequel. Back in July, he showed off another Extraction 3 workout while vacationing in Costa Rica. That session involved a kettlebell, resistance bands and a lengthy circuit of exercises performed in the heat.

The Thailand footage shows another side of his preparation. The earlier routine focused heavily on strength and conditioning. At the same time, these drills emphasize the sort of striking and movement that might come in handy when Tyler Rake inevitably finds himself surrounded by armed men in a hallway. I have a soft spot for the Extraction movies, particularly because director Sam Hargrave seems determined to make every sequel a logistical nightmare for his stunt department.

The original movie in Hargrave's series featured a nearly 12-minute action sequence designed to appear as one continuous shot. Then Extraction 2 arrived in 2023 and delivered an absurdly ambitious 21-minute action sequence involving a prison escape, a moving train and an extremely unfortunate number of people trying to kill the Vacation scene stealer. And, yes, at one point, Tyler Rake was literally on fire.

Hargrave is returning to direct Extraction 3, with Idris Elba set to reprise his role alongside Golshifteh Farahani. David Weil has taken over screenwriting duties from Joe Russo, while the Russo brothers remain involved as producers.

Netflix is still keeping the plot under wraps, though filming has taken the production through Australia and Thailand. Recent set footage has also shown Hemsworth performing action sequences involving boats, so I suspect Tyler Rake will once again spend a significant amount of time being thrown into situations that would kill a normal person.

As of yet, there is no confirmed release date for Extraction 3, as of this writing. The flick also isn't currently listed on Netflix's 2026 streaming release schedule. But don't fret, as fans can revisit the first two movies with a Netflix subscription while waiting for Tyler Rake’s next assignment.

For now, I'm impressed by Hemsworth's commitment. He has already spent years swinging Mjolnir and surviving increasingly ridiculous Extraction set pieces. Seeing him working this hard for a third round makes me excited about what Hargrave has planned. I hope whoever is playing the next villain remembers that the franchise lead has apparently been putting in a lot of time at the office. His office just so happens to be a boxing ring.

#146. How to Watch Live From the Orange Carpet: WNBA Finals

E! is bringing an all-star line-up to the WNBA Finals Oct. 19 with Live From the Orange Carpet, hosted by Lilly Singh, airing on E! and USA, with Game 2 airing on E!, USA and CNBC.

This carpet promises to be nothing but net.

The WNBA Finals will bring the heat as E! presents Live from the Orange Carpet: WNBA Finals Oct. 19, ahead of game two of the championship series between the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries.

Hosted by Lilly Singh, the show tips off live from the Chase Center in San Francisco, as Singh—part owner of the Toronto Tempo—is joined by a starting line-up featuring comedian Wanda Sykes, WNBA legend and Hall of Famer Tina Thompson and WNBA stylist Brittany Hampton.

They will also be joined by USA Sports’ WNBA courtside reporter Terrika Foster-Brasby, who will be giving the full-court press as players like the Dream’s Angel Reese and Jordin Canada, as well as the Valkyries’ Gabby Williams and Veronica Burton arrive at Chase Center.

As for where to watch? The orange carpet is set to be simulcast on E! and USA Network. Then, catch game two immediately after on E!, USA and CNBC.

Viewers will certainly have courtside seats as E! brings its signature award season coverage to the WNBA’s biggest showdown of the year.

“When entertainment is having a moment, Live from E! is there and we’re thrilled to expand that expertise to USA Sports for one of the WNBA’s biggest nights,” Versant Media’s President of Entertainment Val Boreland said. “With Lilly and Wanda and this incredible lineup of talent, Live from the Orange Carpet: WNBA Finals will bring E!’s signature live event coverage and pop culture lens to celebrate the players and cultural influence that make the league so electric both on and off the court.”

Don't miss Live from the Orange Carpet: WNBA Finals on E! and USA Network Oct. 19 at 6 p.m. ET / 3 p.m. PT. Game two of the WNBA finals starts at 8 p.m. ET on E!, USA Network and CNBC.

Until then, for all the behind-the-scenes facts about the WNBA you may not know, read on.

(E!, USA Network and CNBC are all part of the Versant Media family.)

2. When the league first tipped off, there were eight teams total: Charlotte Sting, Cleveland Rockers, Houston Comets, New York Liberty, Los Angeles Sparks, Phoenix Mercury, Sacramento Monarchs and Utah Starzz.

As of the 2026 season, there are 15, with the addition of the Atlanta Dream, Chicago Sky, Connecticut Sun, Dallas Wings, Golden State Valkyries, Indiana Fever, Las Vegas Aces, Minnesota Lynx, Portland Fire, Seattle Storm, Toronto Tempo and Washington Mystics.

However, there have been many pivots in the league's three decades as the Starzz were relocated to San Antonio and then Las Vegas while the Sting, Rockers, Monarchs and Rockets folded. But Tilman Fertitta purchased the Connecticut Sun with plans to rebrand them down in Texas.

3. At the ripe old age of 30, the WNBA is the oldest women's professional sports league in North America.

4. The first ever WNBA game featured the New York Liberty facing the Los Angeles Sparks in L.A.

5. The matchup between two-time champion Lisa Leslie and Olympic gold medalist Rebecca Lobo took place on June 21, 1997.

6. Leslie won back-to-back championship with the Sparks in 2001 and 2002—the same year she recorded the first WNBA in-game dunk.

7. New York Liberty's Teresa Weatherspoon had the first buzzer-beater in an WNBA Finals game in 1999 when she heaved up a shot from beyond half court with less than three seconds left. Though she has said she knew it would go in, "You feel like you're living it in slow motion."

8. Years after she finished her championship-winning college career at Texas Tech, future four-time champ Sheryl Swoops was the first player signed by the WNBA.

9. The three-time MVP also had the league's first triple-double in 1999.

10. Houston Comets forward Tina Thompson was the first WNBA college draft pick, chosen first in the 1997 draft after finishing her run at the University of Southern California.

11. She and her teammates were the first WNBA Champions, defeating the Liberty on Aug. 30, 1997.

12. Houston's point guard Cynthia Cooper was the first WNBA MVP, earning the trophy both in 1997 and 1998.

13. The first WNBA Rookie of the Year was Tracy Reid, the Charlotte Sting guard earning the honors in 1998.

14. Some key stats of WNBA play: Games are played with four quarters that are 10 minutes each.

15. The WNBA season takes place from May until October, with each team playing 44 games.

16. Across 29 seasons, the Seattle Storm, the Minnesota Lynx and the Houston Comets hold the most WNBA Championships, with four a piece.

17. However, Rebekkah Brunson has won a total of five championships—the most of any player—scoring wins with the Sacramento Monarchs in 2005, the Minnesota Lynx in 2011, 2013, 2015 and 2017. She now serves as an assistant coach for the Minneapolis-based squad.

18. Only three current WNBA teams have never won a championship: the Atlanta Dream, Connecticut Sun and Dallas Stars, which selected UConn standout Azzi Fudd with the No. 1 pick in 2026.

19. Candace Parker is the only player to win Rookie of the Year and MVP during the same season in 2008.

20. G'day indeed. Australian Lauren Jackson won two championships with the Storm, four Olympic medals and three MVP honors, making her the first (and, to date, only!) non-American to nab the trophy.

21. Whitney Houston sang the National Anthem at the inaugural WNBA All-Star Game in 1999.

22. Only one WNBA All-Star Game has gone into overtime, when the East defeated the West in 2014.

23. Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson is always a smart bet. She was the first WNBA player to score 1,000-plus points in one season in 2024, the same year she won her third MVP title.

24. She also shares the WNBA single-game scoring record with Liz Cambage, each center knocking in a total of 53 points.

25. With four MVP honors in all, the University of South Carolina alum Wilson has the most in the league, and is a favorite to repeat in 2026.

26. Among her challengers: Indiana Fever's Caitlin Clark, who holds the record for most assists in a single WNBA game at 19.

27. The WNBA all-time leader in points, three-pointers, field goals and free throws, Diana Taurasi—who retired in 2024 after 20 years in Phoenix—is the first WNBA player to hit 1,000 three-point shots, reaching the milestone in 2018.

28. Connecticut Sun center Tina Charles has recorded the most career double-doubles in WNBA history with 194.

29. Sue Bird is the only WNBA player to net three championship titles in three different decades, the retired point guard raising the trophy with her Seattle teammates in 2004, 2010, 2018 and 2020.

30. Sometimes that's just the way the ball bounces. The longest game in WNBA history went into quadruple overtime in 2001.

Other Mommy may be going down as one of the most disappointing 2026 releases, but a lot of us saw it in honor of it being the prime season for horror movies. The Blumhouse-Atomic Monster flick was met with savage reviews, but it’s been a box office success that even led to a funny text exchange between Jessica Chastain and a The Social Reckoning star. Now, I need to talk about that ending, because there’s a lot more to it than I thought. SPOILERS AHEAD!

There are a lot of Other Mommy issues, particularly with the tone. But the nail in the coffin for me was the finale. I didn’t hate the bit where Jessica Chastain’s Ursula tells her daughter Bela the truth that her Daddo isn’t her biological father. Or Bela getting the strength to take on Other Mommy herself by tricking her, but by the final frame it’s never clear if Bela successfully fights her off or not. The movie ends with an unclever *wink wink* that just frustrates me.

A ton of movies have been able to tackle the ambiguous ending, but Other Mommy was so vague from beginning to end that having this kind of conclusion made me want to throw popcorn at the screen. Especially because the whole movie has us following a scared eight-year-old child the whole time. If you’re going to break my heart, do it; don’t tease it without being clear about it, you know? I felt like I was being ghosted by a date I barely liked. Icky!

Check out the book Other Mommy is based on, Incidents Around The House, right now.

The frustrating ending led me to dig into the book based on the movie, Incidents Around the House. I had heard really good things about the novel by Josh Malerman, and I couldn’t believe the film could have followed the same plotline. What I found out is that while it does very much have the same setup that grabbed me from the beginning about Other Mommy, the movie made a huge change to the ending.

Rather than there being a cryptic result around whether Bela defeats Other Mommy and her parents survive, things are very different. In the book, Other Mommy not only kills her Grandma Ruth, but Bela’s parents, too. Ultimately, an isolated and traumatized Bela agrees to let Other Mommy “into her heart”. The ending sees Bela finding herself in a dark, seemingly infinite space where all she can hear is Other Mommy practicing her voice and then embodying her now with a human subject to possess.

I mean… given, it's a lot more brutal, but it’s worlds better than the ending we get in my opinion. I wonder if they shot the original ending and this was a complaint in test screenings they ultimately decided to move away from? I get the filmmakers perhaps not wanting to leave audiences with a child being possessed by the end, but it is an R-rated horror movie after all. Softening the blow with the finale didn’t make it better. It just made me mad.

Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

#148. See Who the WNBA's Angel Reese & More Athletes Have Teamed Up With IRL

As Angel Reese, DeWanna Bonner and other Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries athletes shoot their shot in the WNBA finals, we're sharing the teammates they huddle up with off the court.

Come Oct. 21, NBA center Wendell Carter Jr. will be facing quite the double-team. Because an hour after his Orlando Magic are set to tip off against the Atlanta Hawks in Florida, his real-life MVP Angel Reese will be pressing her way down the court some 440 miles away in Georgia.

So, while it'd take more than a little, uh, magic for the 27-year-old to huddle up with his girlfriend, 24, in game three of the Atlanta Dream's WNBA finals campaign against the Golden State Valkyries, he provided quite the assist in his off-season.

"A lot of hard work, a lot of relaxation, a lot of support for my girl," the Duke alum recently told Brandon “Scoop B” Robinson of his game plan. "It's been a great summer all in all."

And while he can't go full-court press for Reese—who's competing for the Dream after two seasons in Chicago—he's always on her proverbial bench.

"We're both competitors," Carter explained of their shared mindset. "Before games, after games, we tell each other what we should do night in and night out and not to pay too much attention to the outside noise. We call it the white noise."

Of course, Reese, who earned an NCAA championship while at Louisiana State University, isn't the only athlete with a key teammate in her corner.

Before DeWanna Bonner joined the Dream in August, she was competing for the Phoenix Mercury alongside fiancée Alyssa Thomas.

And while the two certainly like to dunk on each other ("She's not getting a bucket," Thomas cracked before they faced off during the 2024 WNBA All-Star festivities), such rivalries only up their game play.

"I love playing with Alyssa," Bonner detailed in their 2024 cover interview for SLAM Magazine. "She's one of the hardest working competitors in the League, so it kind of makes me want to go harder."

And, no doubt, as she hits the hardwood with her squad, no one will be cheering louder than her future bride. We've got the stats on their partnership and the real-life teammates other WNBA stars spend their time huddled up with.

"I think the next time I'll post I'm in a relationship is when I'm married," WNBA standout Angel Reese shared during a January 2025 episode of her Unapologetically Angel podcast, explaining a newfound desire for privacy. "You might see me on a date. You gonna have to catch me though. Like, I’m not gonna post a man on my page."

Still, there have been definitive clues that the Bayou Barbie has found her Ken in Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. "That’s a sign," the Atlanta Dream power forward captioned a TikTok showcasing an impressive arrangements of roses, "that’s a signnnn." And it was certainly a big play when the Duke alum turned up to the 2025 WNBA All-Star game sporting a t-shirt baring Reese's visage.

The NCAA champ—set to appear on season two of The Hunting Wives—returned the favor, attending a December 2025 Magic game in a jersey emblazoned with the words "My Man."

Game recognizes game, and three-time WNBA champion A'ja Wilson has found her ace of hearts in Bam Adebayo.

The low-key couple first sparked dating rumors in the summer of 2024, and Wilson confirmed their romance with a bit of a pump fake when she showed up at NBA All Star Weekend in February 2025.

"My NBA All-Star is not here," the Las Vegas Aces center told People, acknowledging that the Miami Heat center hadn't made the roster. But Adebayo was busy "getting the rest he needs," she added, "and that's the best Valentine gift that I can truly give him, is just the rest."

And they're only heating up, Adebayo showing up to support Wilson—who made her fifth straight All-Star team—during the WNBA All-Star festivities in July 2025.

Months later, in her TIME Athlete of the Year cover story, she revealed they'd actually been huddled up way longer than fans realized, making that first move at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021.

Next up: Adding to their squad. "That is always a dream," she said of having kids with Adebayo. "This is my life partner. Honestly, what on earth was my world before you? That’s how much he’s impacted my life, my family’s life."

Sabrina Ionescu has racked up an impressive haul of trophies playing for the New York Liberty, WNBA All-Stars and U.S. Olympic team, but the day she married NFL player Hroniss Grasu is especially close to her heart.

"March 10, 2024. The day I got to marry my best friend, my other half," she captioned her Instagram wedding photo. "The best day of my life."

Marta Xargay Casademont & Breanna Stewart

Three-time WNBA champion Breanna Stewart met her love match with Spanish basketball player Marta Xargay Casademont. They connected as teammates on a Russian professional women's basketball team in 2018 and got engaged and married in 2021. They welcomed their first child Ruby in August 2021, followed by their son Theo in October 2023.

Xargay Casademont retired from the sport in 2021, but continues to support her wife's career, writing on Instagram after Stewart's New York Liberty won the 2024 Finals, "So freaking proud of you!"

Indiana Fever megastar Caitlin Clark has been dating basketball player and former Butler University assistant coach Connor McCaffery since April 2023.

The pair haven't been shy about celebrating their love on social media, with McCaffery posting a sweet birthday tribute for his girlfriend's January 2025 birthday: "You have an incredible ability to inspire and lift up those around you, and I am lucky to learn from you every day. Thank you for always being you. I love you."

New York Liberty shooting guard and 2021 WNBA All-Star Betnijah Laney is married to fellow basketball player Jordan Hamilton, who started for the Denver Nuggets, New Orleans Pelicans, and Houston Rockets during his NBA career.

In an Instagram tribute for their second wedding anniversary in 2023, Laney wrote, "Your arms are my favorite place to be."

After dating for eight years, Diana Taurasi married her Phoenix Mercury teammate Penny Taylor on May 13, 2017. Now both retired from the sport, the iconic WNBA couple have more time to spend with their children, Leo and Isla.

After a few weeks of speculation, Dallas Wings point guard Paige Bueckers confirmed in July 2025 that she was dating Azzi Fudd, her former teammate on the UConn’s women’s basketball team.

And with Fudd selected first overall by the Wings in the 2026 draft, the two were thrilled to pair up on and off the hardwood. "I'm excited to play again with Paige," Fudd told ESPN during draft night April 13. "She's an incredible person. An incredible player, and it's gonna be a lot of fun."

Prior to playing for the Indiana Fever in 2024 and re-joining the Seattle Storm in February 2025, Katie Lou Samuelson was busy with her life off the court. She married basketball player Devin Cannady in April 2023 and the couple announced the birth of their daugher Aliya in August 2023.

WNBA superstar Napheesa Collier can add devoted wife and mom to her long list of achievements (which includes two Olympic gold medals and 2025 All-Star Game MVP).

In October 2019, the Minnesota Lynx forward got engaged to basketball skills coach Alex Bazzell and they were married three years later. In 2022, they welcomed daughter Mila Sarah Bazzell.

Then-Chicago Sky teammates Allie Quigley and Courtney Vandersloot were married in December 2018 and share daughter Jana, who was born on April 8, 2025.

The winning pair are not only the first married couple to win a professional sports championship together (the 2021 WNBA Finals), but in May 2025, a month before Quigley announced her retirement, Vandersloot surpassed her wife's record as the all-time leading scorer for the Chicago Sky.

In March 2021, Alyssa Thomas shared on social media that she was dating her then-Connecticut Sun teammate, DeWanna Bonner.

The pair got engaged in 2023 when Thomas proposed during the WNBA All-Star Weekend. Bonner is also mom to Cali and Demi, the twins she welcomed in 2017 with ex-wife and former Phoenix Mercury teammate Candice Dupree.

Just when I thought last year’s Academy Museum Gala was a smash with Cara Delevingne sparking in silver or Emily Ratajkowski’s floating-shoulders look, A-listers brought their A-game once again this year. At the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala, Taylor Swift looked like a princess wearing a pale blue Dior gown, and Janelle Monáe literally spread her butterfly wings in a purple Robert Wun ensemble. But I’ve got to say my personal favorite had to be Charlize Theron’s barely-there dress, though I still loved Sabrina Carpenter’s tassels look as well.

Theron truly showed off her true fashionista status this year for The Odyssey's red carpet, wearing a silver fringe gown at the China premiere and a high-slit dress with over-the-top gloves at the London event. But, at the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala in Los Angeles, the Academy Award winner was a total standout at the event, wearing a barely-there dress that brought bold and edgy in the best way:

The model-turned-actress’ sheer black Tom Ford gown was the perfect blend of elegance and daring. With the black bodice featuring geometrically detailed lace panels and a sheer skirt that revealed a lot of leg, Theron proved that the alluring element of sheer can reveal just enough to make a statement and still be classy. And her arrow earring makes her look like such a warrior!

If you thought the Apex star looked like a gem at the gala, take a look below at more Old Hollywood-level photos Theron shared on her Instagram:

A post shared by Charlize Theron (@charlizeafrica)

Whether the Monster actress is posing on the couch or out on the balcony, doesn’t it look like she’s giving Grace Kelly vibes? Theron is radiating confidence and poise in this Tom Ford ensemble in a way that only she can. In the caption of her post, she muses that she's considered a "legend," and I can't disagree.

Theron’s barely-there gown may have been a true knockout for me, but Sabrina Carpenter's look was also on my radar. During the festivities, the Grammy winner dazzled at the Academy Museum Gala donning a cobalt dress with draping tassels, which really made it a showstopper:

The “Espresso” singer has already been known for looking retro-glam and playful, like her Met Gala little black dress this year. But her Academy Museum Gala look is one I can’t take my eyes off of. She was perfectly rocking the blue Giorgio Armani Privé gown as it draped down to the floor.

However, the key feature of that glamorous dress was its tassel straps swung over her shoulders, revealing Carpenter's open back. I’m honestly curious as to how the dress managed to stay on as the tassels seemingly hung freely from her shoulders. Nevertheless, leave it to the former Disney Channel star to pull off that unique look with such flair and conviction.

Based on the distinctive dresses of Charlize Theron and Sabrina Carpenter alone, the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala showcased grace with individuality. Yet others, including Teyana Taylor, also donned great outfits for the night. Like their peers, Carpenter and Theron proved that chic and modern boldness can go hand-in-hand, leading to a person slaying the red carpet in the process.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#150. Why Kylie Jenner Was Chosen to Wear Victoria's Secret Fantasy Bra

Kylie Jenner became the first non-Victoria's Secret Angel to model the lingerie brand's iconic Fantasy Bra during the 2026 VS Fashion Show on Oct. 18. Here's why she was chosen.

Kylie Jenner is keeping up with the Angels.

The Kardashians star made made her Victoria's Secret Fashion Show debut on Oct. 18, becoming the first non-Angel to model the famed Fantasy Bra after the lingerie piece's eight-year absence from the catwalk.

In donning the $50 million bustier—which featured a yellow diamond centerpiece worth $22 million alone, as well as 4,410 other natural diamonds—she joined the ranks of past models such as Gisele Bündchen, Heidi Klum, Tyra Banks, Adriana Lima, Alessandra Ambrosio and Candice Swanepoel who were bestowed the prestigious runway honor.

So, why did Victoria's Secret choose to Jenner for this year's show-stopping moment?

“Kylie really extends beyond fashion, beyond culture, beyond TV, beyond one singular thing,” Victoria's Secret chief creative officer Adam Selman explained in a Vogue interview published Oct. 18. “That’s the exact same thing that we do. Like, the show is so big, it’s true entertainment, and I think that she is a great catalyst for that."

"She’s really created her own culture, which—how many people can say that?" he continued, explaining that the "big idea for the show was fandomonium."

"I think it’s an interesting pairing that we’re giving the fans: we’re giving them what they want with this amazing Fantasy Bra, and we’re going to put it on an unexpected talent who has a massive following and massive cultural impact," Selman added. "I think it’s fun. I think it’s really joyful, and I think it’s fun to celebrate in a different way that people aren’t going to expect."

And this year's Fantasy Bra was, according to Selmam, "almost museum quality."

Weighing just a little under 4 lbs., the bra took 15 Jacob & Co. craftspeople more than 1,000 hours to build it.

“Remember, this bra is made entirely of gold and diamonds—there is no fabric," designer Jacob Arabo told Vogue. "So getting the right fit and making sure it could move naturally with the body was not easy.”

That's why he said the "biggest challenge was making sure the bra was comfortable to wear while keeping true to the design."

“Even with exact measurements, what looks good on paper doesn’t always work the same way on the body,” Arabo continued. “Every curve, every diamond, and every piece of gold had to be carefully placed so the bra would be both beautiful and comfortable.”

But for Jenner, who was cheered on by boyfriend Timothée Chalamet and Kris Jenner during her walk down the runway, she and the Fantasy Bra were a match made in heaven. As the 29-year-old captioned a close-up herself wearing the bra in an Oct. 18 Instagram Story, "BEST DAY EVER."

More is obviously better when it comes to box office, but winning is a complicated game in Hollywood. It’s not always just about the big number reported every weekend. Sometimes it’s about the little numbers that lead up to and play into that big number, and for one movie this weekend, those little numbers are telling a really exciting story.

The clear number one at the box office this weekend is Street Fighter. The video game adaptation is currently estimated to take home more than $30,000,000 during its debut, but it’s the Nathan Fielder led documentary You Can See Everything that has the best story to tell. Documentaries, at least those that don’t involve a Taylor Swift concert or a Michael Moore expose, aren’t typically the type to get people to the theater. More often than not, they find their audience on streaming, but You Can See Everything is looking like the rare documentary that is going to break through.

The A24 flick, which is directed by Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, was reportedly made for around $7,000,000 and is now poised to take home $15,000,000 this weekend. That’s well beyond the estimates we’ve seen the last few weeks, and it’s a spectacular number compared to the number of screens it’s actually showing on. Street Fighter, as a comparison, opened on over 3500 screens this weekend. You Can See Everything, on the other hand, opened on just 855. That means Street Fighter is going to make between $8,000 and $9,000 per screen this weekend, while You Can See Everything is going to make between $17,000 and $18,000.

You can check out the full weekend estimates after the Friday and Saturday grosses according to The Numbers…

I know I’ve glossed over Street Fighter here a bit, but those involved with the movie should do at least some celebrating. With a production budget rumored to be in the $80M range, it has a long ways to go before it’ll turn a profit, but winning a weekend at the box office is not easy. Every single victory is hard fought, and there are clearly a lot of people who wanted to see the new adaptation and are largely finding it dumb but also fun. If it can only drop in the 50% or so range next weekend and pick up some healthy chunks in foreign markets, it could wind up producing enough to get a sequel.

As for the rest of the box office, there wasn’t a ton of good news to go around. Other Mommy had the drop off everyone expected thanks to the poor reviews and poor word of mouth. Whalefall and Sense and Sensibility both made the top five but weren’t able to top $10M, which is probably the numbers they needed to feel like solid hits. The Social Reckoning and Digger also continued to disappoint, as neither made the top ten.

It’ll be interesting to see what A24 decides to do with You Can See Everything, which is getting fantastic reviews and responses. These numbers are the type that normally convince a studio to expand wider, but given the genre and the three hour runtime, A24 may decide to stick to less screens and a more specialized rollout. Regardless, this weekend was great news for the film, even if it lost the weekend.

#152. Heated Rivalry's Ksenia Kharlamova Details Filming Season 2

Heated Rivalry star Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova shared a glimpse into working on season two of the hockey romance during an exclusive E! News interview at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show.

Filming Heated Rivalry season two has been an unrivaled experience.

Just ask Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova. After all, the actress reflected on returning to the steamy hockey romance alongside costars Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie, plus a new ensemble of characters from Rachel Reid's Game Changers universe.

"It's still very grounded and fun and light-hearted," Kharlamova exclusively told E! News at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show on Oct. 18. "It's just fun being on the set. All the new cast members are so fun.”

While Williams and Storrie are bringing Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov back to life, respectively, Justice Smith is making his Heated Rivalry debut as social media manager Harris Drover for Ottawa—a.k.a. Ilya's new team—opposite Charlie Gillespie's hockey player Troy Barrett.

Other new additions include Daniel Diemer as Toronto's Ryan Price, his love interest Fabian Salah (Shaheen Jafargholi) and Emily Hampshire as Fabian's BFF Vanessa.

"It's awesome," Kharlamova—who plays Ilya's best friend Svetlana Vetrova—added. "It's changed it for the better. It's like having more friends there."

The model couldn't help but praise the show's director and creator Jacob Tierney, adding that he is "just such a great person to be around."

Although Kharlamova admitted that she couldn't share any more details about filming, Tierney previously revealed how Svetlana ultimately has continued to become a “more rounded and important character” in the series.

"I do think that telling an honest story about queer men involves female allies because that's our lives, especially when you're young," he told the audience at the A Night of Heated Rivalry in Brooklyn earlier this month. But he added, with Ilya, "because he's so internal. I was like, 'You need to talk to somebody.'"

And fans will get to see more of the best friends in the upcoming installment, which is set to premiere in spring 2027.

"This happens a lot in season two, where he's lying, but at least he's saying something out loud," Tierney continued. "It's so interesting to have to watch him call her and be like, 'I'm fine. I love it here.' You're like, 'OK, well, you're not.'"

Devens and his sidekick Drew had to tell Dee a few truths.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

At this point Rick Devens has become the winningest Big Brother contestant amongst all Big Brother houseguests. He’s achieved a feat, and he did so by establishing and maintaining a slew of interpersonal relationships in the house, becoming a fan favorite, and winning competitions in several key moments when he otherwise would have gone home. His Survivor pal Dee played a bolder game, and made more enemies during her tenure. Since her exit, there’s been a lot that’s been written about her friending then unfriending the Pipe Queen Mallory.

While I didn’t expect to see these petty interactions go down outside of the house, perhaps I should have. I just keep flashing back to this clip of Dee, Drew, and Devens when it was later days in the competition. At one point, Dee mentioned she’d love to be friends with Mallory outside of the show, and Drew and Devens had to break it to her: That was never going to happen.

dee: i wanna get to know mallory more, i feel like we never had the chance.. devens: i dont think you're gonna have the chance dee: really? outside of here too? devens: she dont seem like the forgiving type.. i dont think shes gonna want to know us.. #bb28 https://t.co/CY0XjIkOW1September 23, 2026

In the clip from the Big Brother 28 live feeds, Dee said she’s really like to get to know Mallory outside of the house. (And not in the same way Drew seems like he'd like to get to know Melody.) Drew and Devens were basically like, “Oh girl, that’s not going to happen” after Dee was honest with Mallory she was going to put her up. In fact, Devens specifically told Dee he didn’t feel she was “the forgiving type.”

This was before any of them had actually left the house and seen Mallory’s full-on rage about her situation before and after her CBS exit. It’s also before her big mad reaction to Devens saving himself went viral mid-season. She was vocal that she did not like Dee in the Diary room while still on the show, though she later told Gold Derby and other outlets she did “not dislike” Dee.

Here's how Mallory handled her exit press, and what she said about Dee and not hating her on "on a personal level.”

[I do not hate her] on a personal level. I do think this was a bad game move. It’s hard to not be emotional about it when it’s your dream to be there and you’re being betrayed! And you know, someone’s the reason that your dream is ending when it’s what you wanted your whole life. And you know, they were just recruited from Survivor. That’s a whole nother story. But I don’t hate her on a personal level.

She also took to X to explain her actual position about what was going on during Big Brother and did repeat there that she did not “hate anyone.”

Everyone can think what they want. While the show is going on and my friends are in there I am emotionally invested because I care about them. I’m allowed to root for my friends and it’s hard to watch hurtful things happen to people you care about. Anyone who has been on the show would understand that and it will be fine when it’s all over. I don’t hate anyone.

However, after Dee left the house, she clearly didn't feel the same. The two women had followed one another on Instagram, but an unfriending brouhaha between Mallory and the former Survivor player captured the Internet’s attention. Dee publicly unfollowed Mallory, and fans online certainly noticed. So, while Mallory may be over it or allegedly over it, there’s some real beef there. I also wonder if Dee having this realization with Drew and Devens may have led her to feel justified to unfriend Mallory, too, but that’s neither here nor there..

This is hardly the only Big Brother feud to ever happen, and it won’t be the last. Part of the problem with bringing in Dee and Devens from another franchise is that their style of gameplay was new and unusual for the house. Dee gave advice to CinemaBlend about how to play Big Brother that I think encapsulates everything Mallory disliked about them coming into the game. There was always naturally going to be some friction inside the house. I’m just a little surprised it followed them out of it.

#154. Selena Gomez Says Vaping Nicotine Changed Her Voice

Selena Gomez shared her voice has been permanently changed from frequently vaping nicotine: “It’s just not worth it. It’s so stupid.”

Selena Gomez wants fans to know her bad habit is not good for you, either.

The Rare Beauty founder detailed her struggles with vaping nicotine, sharing her voice has been permanently changed due to prolonged use.

“I’m not gonna be able to change my voice,” Gomez explained in a video posted on her Instagram Stories Oct. 18. “I vaped nicotine a lot, and just so everyone knows that's somewhat vaped.”

“Nicotine is so hard to quit,” she continued. “I think I just wanted to say if you're going through it, or if you're even trying to vape, it's just not worth it. It’s so stupid.”

“It’s changed my voice,” Gomez added. “So if you guys don't like listening to my voice, that's totally understandable. I don't mind. Just don't listen to it.”

But the “Good For You” singer shared that she’s been able to quit her habit.

“I am really excited because I stopped,” she said, “and I just hope I can keep it up. It's really hard.”

And the Only Murders in the Building star concluded her video by sharing an inspirational message for others who may be struggling.

“I know if you are going through something, you can get through it too,” Gomez said. “It sucks.”

Gomez has previously opened up about her voice experiencing changes, though due to other factors.

Indeed, last year, the “Calm Down” singer addressed fan concern about her voice, pointing to side effects from her medications used to treat lupus and bipolar disorder.

“I’ve gotten this question a few times. Sometimes, when I’m on…nevermind, there’s no excuse,” she shared during an Instagram Live in December 2025. “I don’t really care. I think my point is that things happen.”

“My throat kind of swells on the inside sometimes,” she added. “That’s all.”

But Gomez expressed gratitude to her fans for bringing the topic to her attention.

“I’m glad you’re being real with me on the Live,” she noted. “I appreciate it.”

Despite the 34-year-old’s voice potentially being forever altered, there are other changes she’s happy to welcome into her life, specifically the effects of getting older.

“I don’t feel like it’s a bad thing,” Gomez told People in an interview published Sept. 16. “Getting older has been so fun. I’m not scared at all. I love getting older. Things are going to change and things are going to sag, but you’re alive. I think age is just a number in many ways.”

Nobody knows how to rock a look like Zendaya, and her stylist, Law Roach, truly outdid himself for The Odyssey's press tour. From Sophia Webster gladiator sandals, to flowy custom Jacquemus she wore in London, Zendaya truly looked like a real life Greek goddess. However, one of the fan-favorite red carpet looks inspired by the Greek epic was hands-down the Schiaparelli breastplate that made her look like a statue. Recently, Teyana Taylor rocked a similar look, showing the breastplate structured gowns are having a moment right now.

Taylor attended the 6th annual Academy Museum Gala and looked like an absolute star. She wore a baby blue Schiaparelli gown with a breastplate with a sheer floral skirt that is from the Fall/Winter 2026 Couture collection. Her pixie cut allows the dress and her face to have its own moment, and the dress is truly a remarkable work of art. You can see her full look below:

It’s a stunning look, and it’s hard not to see the stark similarities between this fit and Zendaya’s very own breastplate look. The Spider-Man star's was also Schiaparelli and her look was from the same collection as Taylor’s, which is likely why they were so similar. Zendaya’s, however, was white and had more sparkle in the skirt. All in all, it represented yet another instance of the star method-dressing for a project. You can see the Dune lead's look from the London premiere of The Odyssey below:

Even though these looks are similar, I think both stars are really rocking them in their own right. This feels less like a copy cat situation and more like a trend forming. Schiaparelli's structured looks are having a real moment right now, as the brand is becoming a favorite of Kylie Jenner, Lady Gaga and Beyoncé. They are known for their sculptural bodices and many people are embracing breastplates for more of an avant garde look.

For example, Lupita Nyongo’ wore a silver breastplate to the Tony Awards in 2023 that was molded to her body. Jennifer Lopez also wore a half-breastplate to the Elle Women In Hollywood event she attended with Ben Affleck also in 2023. However, if we were to trace this trend back, it’s hard to ignore that the true origin of the high-fashion breastplate in modern red carpet fashion starts with Zendaya. The Euphoria star famously wore a Tom Ford breastplate to the Critics Choice Awards in 2020, and it really set the tone for this being a major trend. The Shrek 5 star even revealed she had it framed in her house, which couldn’t be cooler.

I guess when it comes to a Zendaya look, you can’t really go wrong, so it’s no surprise that someone like Teyana Taylor would want to take a note out of the Emmy winner’s fashion bible. The best part is they both look incredible, and I hope to see more of these sculptural looks on the red carpet as celebs get bolder with their fashion choices.

Fans can see Zendaya in The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which are both at the end of their theatrical runs, so make sure to check them out on the big screen while you still can. She'll also appear in Dune: Part Three, which hits the 2026 movie schedule on December 18 and, hopefully, she'll rock some sweet fits during that press tour. Fans of Teyana Taylor can see her in her Oscar-nominated performance in One Battle After Another, which is streaming now with a HBO Max subscription.

#156. Why Law Roach Is Asking Fans to Let Zendaya “Live for a Second”

Zendaya's stylist Law Roach joked that fans need to let the actress "live for a second" after a busy year in an exclusive E! News interview at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show Oct. 18.

Zendaya's had quite the odyssey in the past year.

That's why her stylist Law Roach believes the actress deserves a break after embarking on a whirlwind promotional tour for The Odyssey, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Drama following her wedding to husband Tom Holland.

"Zendaya is busy," Roach exclusively told E! News at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show on Oct. 18. "She's had a lot this year. Y'all, give my sister a break. Let her rest. Let her live for a second."

Besides, Zendaya isn't done with her year of method dressing just yet. After all, Dune: Part Three is set to hit theaters in December, meaning there'll be more dramatic red carpet fashion moments coming soon.

"She is preparing for the Dune 3 press tour, so am I," Roach continued. "So, she's resting."

But that's not to say the 48-year-old has stopped working. In fact, he's still booked a busy styling Kim Kardashian.

"She's incredible—just sweet, nice, happy," Roach raved of the Kardashians star. "I love working with happy. Everyone I work with now are happy, and I'm happy. I just love being in a happy place."

So much so, the Project Runway judge is thinking about starting an acting career. a personal goal he's already discussed with Zendaya.

"She said, 'Acting is reacting,'" he shared, "and when she told me, I was like, 'Oh, I understand that because you're reacting to what the other person is giving you.'"

There's clearly a lot of hard feelings here.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Between in-person events, podcast appearances, watch parties and more, the community of former Survivor players has never felt so interconnected. It’s obvious there’s a close affinity between many castaways and a particularly special bond amongst multi-time players and legends of the game. Unfortunately, it’s also become clear over the last few years that the aforementioned closeness doesn’t always extend to longtime host Jeff Probst and the producers, and if there was any doubt about that friction, beloved fan favorites Tyson Apostol and Parvati Shallow ripped off that band-aid.

If you’re plugged into the Survivor community on social media, you’ve no doubt noticed it over the last few years. There’s been an undercurrent of negativity directed toward Jeff and the producers from many former players. Some of it has been about the format of the show and gameplay related decisions, and those squabbles have felt healthy and entirely normal. Those of us who love Survivor should have different opinions about game mechanics and three tribes versus two.

Unfortunately, a lot of it has gone beyond that and felt very personal. It’s obvious there are legitimate hard feelings amongst many former players. Some of that has been about the show’s casting process. Probst and the producers promised Survivor 50 would honor the legacy of the show. More than a hundred former players were reportedly contacted to participate, but some of the biggest names in the history of the show apparently didn’t even get a basic check-in or didn't get one until they complained on social.

Some of those who were contacted later said they felt deceived or lied to by producers who allegedly told them them to clear their schedules because they were locks to be cast, only to cut them later. One popular former player made it to the end of the casting process and was allegedly never even informed she was cut.

In addition, Probst made some negative comments about former players going on other reality competition shows. He made it clear that unless you’re a Cirie-style legend of the game, if you go on The Traitors, Big Brother, House Of Villains or other similar programs, it will be held against you in the casting process. Both fans and former players very loudly pushed back on his comments, to the point where Jeff actually came out and apologized and said his perspective was wrong.

Let the record show that apology has definitely not fixed the issue with everyone though. Parvati was a guest on Tyson’s podcast The Pod Has Spoken this week. The two talked about how much they’re enjoying Survivor 51 and the so-called Open Era. Much of the conversation was quite positive, but when the subject of returning to Survivor came up, it got a lot more negative. Tyson made it clear he’s very unlikely to ever return, and Parvati said there’s not any amount of money that would get her back on the US version.

Parvati was reluctant to talk about specifics and said people should read between the lines, but she did eventually offer a few thoughts. She said she’s still frustrated about Jeff saying he’s less likely to cast people who have been on other shows and said it’s particularly frustrating that Survivor pretends some people like Boston Rob, Michele Fitzgerald, Dee, Rick Devens, Cirie, Tyson and herself aren’t born to compete and go on these shows. She also said she doesn’t feel like those involved with the show treat her with the “kindness” she feels she deserves.

I just want to be treated with kindness and respect. That’s it. That’s all I ask for. That’s what I give to others.

Tyson was clearly on board with her comments and said he feels the same way. He, however, put it in more practical terms. He said Survivor has this weird perspective on loyalty that even if they’re not paying you, you should remain committed to Survivor and be loyal in case they want to use you again in the future. He said that’s particularly frustrating because the show doesn’t pay very well and doesn’t even pretend to be thankful for your contributions.

Other shows pay way more. They say, ‘Thank you. We couldn’t have done this without you’ rather than ‘you’re welcome for the opportunity.’ Your welcome for the opportunity doesn’t feel as good as thank you. We couldn’t have done this without you.

I have no idea what Survivor’s finances look like, and I’m not going to comment on whether they should be paying bigger appearance fees for returning players. That’s a decision way above my paygrade, but I will say that Probst and company need to figure out how to mend fences with a lot of these former players. If it was just one or two, I wouldn’t necessarily draw the conclusion that it was the fault of production, but when so many players consistently make negative comments and say they’ve been treated poorly, it feels like a larger pattern.

Even if they don't actually play again, I want a world where Tyson and Parvati and legends like them make the occasional appearance on the show or during a finale or on an official podcast. I want a world where players going through the casting process feel like they're being treated fairly and honestly. I want a world in which the best players on Survivor go crush other shows like Dee and Devens on Big Brother and Cirie and Carolyn on The Traitors and then return back to their original home. I want a world in which there's more positivity around Survivor.

#158. Megan Moroney Reveals Her Underwear Fell Off on Red Carpet

Megan Moroney shared her underwear once fell off while on a red carpet of an awards show during an exclusive interview with E! News at the 2026 VS Fashion Show Oct. 18.

Megan Moroney is still doing OK—even if she’s going commando.

Indeed, the country star detailed the shocking fashion moment in which she once took off her underwear on the red carpet of an awards show.

When asked by E! News at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show Oct. 18 about her most “outrageous” risk she's taken for fashion, Moroney replied, “I’ll tell you what my brain immediately went to. The ACM Awards a few years ago, I had these like sticky underwear on, and they fell off on the carpet.”

“So then I just took them off and gave them to my publicist,” she added. “So yeah, I didn't have underwear on carpet.”

And though the “Am I Okay?” singer did not reveal her undergarment situation on the pink carpet at the event, she did shed light on what makes her feel “sexiest.”

As Moroney—who donned a red, chainlink minidress at the VS Fashion Show—simply put it, “When I’m in an outfit like this.”

And her key to confidence? The “I Feel Pretty” artist feels best when she’s being herself.

“I think just embracing who I am, embracing my individuality,” Moroney shared, “we're all unique.”

Indeed, the 29-year-old showed off that confidence when she performed on the runway at the iconic fashion event, singing three of her songs from her latest album Cloud 9: “6 Months Later,” “Wish I Didn’t” and “Sorry…I Meant Tonight.”

And for her performance, Moroney’s look didn’t feature any Tennessee orange in sight. After all, the “No Caller ID” artist donned a Victoria’s Secret pink babydoll corset and skirt, paired with silver platform sandals, completing the ensemble by wearing fluffy pink wings.

But Moroney taking the legendary stage aligns perfectly with her new era in more ways than one.

In fact, along with Cloud 9—which was released in February—featuring a hot pink cover and aesthetic, it reflects her entering a new, confident era in her life.

“It’s still strong and empowering, but there is a softness to a lot of the lyrics,” she shared at a 2025 promotional event, per Music Mayhem Magazine. “And I think that comes with the confidence that I’ve had that’s grown inside me over the past however many months that I’ve made this album. So it’s just me living life.”

Last week marked the end of Guillermo Rodriguez’s Dancing with the Stars journey, as he and dance partner Witney Carson were eliminated at the conclusion of Week 5 of Season 35. During his tenure on the reality competition series amid the 2026 TV schedule, Guillermo became a fan-favorite and amassed a lot of support, despite not receiving high scores. On that note, his talk show partner, Jimmy Kimmel, paid tribute to him after his elimination and, as sweet as it was on air, it turns out there are some even lovelier BTS details.

Kimmel paid tribute to his longtime sidekick’s DWTS run during his opening monologue on the October 14th broadcast of Jimmy Kimmel Live!, and it was quite sentimental. While the host began by questioning Guillermo about what he might do with his newfound reality TV fame, Kimmel segued into a sweet montage chronicling the ups and downs of his buddy’s stint on Dancing. Later, Carson came out before the audience, and she and Guillermo danced. Carson later discussed the tribute, and shared behind-the-scenes insights:

I was really sad, I actually just came from Jimmy Kimmel, and they had a huge montage of our journey together. And all the producers were crying, and the audience did a full standing ovation. And I’ve got chills, I got so emotional, so today I’m feeling mixed emotions.

Carson – who’s currently pregnant with her third child – made these comments while speaking with ET (as seen on Instagram), and they’re so sweet. And, while viewers at home got some shots of the audience cheering, I love knowing that they all came together to give Carson and Guillermo a standing ovation. Check out the tribute during the monologue below:

The last leg of Guillermo and Carson’s DWTS stint was Super Bowl Night, which saw the pair perform a salsa routine to Bad Bunny’s “Tití Me Preguntó”. Ultimately, the two earned their highest score of the competition – a 22 out of 40. That ranking, however, was still low compared to the scores of their competitors and, by the time the night was over, their names were called during the elimination portion of the night.

Overall, Guillermo’s time on Dancing was filled with both highs and lows, from the army of fans who supported him on social media to those who were mad about him avoiding elimination despite low scores. There was also the supposedly shady comment from fellow competitor Jackson Olson regarding one of Rodriguez’s routines, though Olson later publicly apologized for that.

There was certainly a lot of anticipation for Guillermo’s involvement in DWTS after he was initially announced as a competitor. Needless to say, his tenure on the long-running series didn’t disappoint, and Guillermo himself expressed gratitude for his time on the program following his elimination. I love that he’s thankful for having had the opportunity to compete and that both he and Witney Carson got their flowers on Jimmy Kimmel’s show in such a sweet way.

It’s that time of year folks, the time of year when new programs have returned to the fall TV schedule and people are settling into their viewing habits. Unfortunately for me, I think that’s very bad news for one brand new TV series. Yes, it’s only been a few weeks and I’m already concerned my favorite new fall TV show is gonna get the old cancelation axe.

Which fall show am I talking about? None other than newbie Line of Fire.

Here’s the gist. Every fall I usually try to watch the pilot at least for most of the new fall TV slate. Sometimes I’ll pick up shows for the whole season afterward; other times I won’t. This year, I was really intrigued by Peter Krause’s latest Line of Fire, an NBC family drama set in the realm of law enforcement that’s straight up giving Blue Bloods vibes. I’ve been avidly watching. However, things have not been totally rosy for the newcomer.

So far, Line of Fire has aired four episodes. The fifth hits the network on Monday night. The show honestly kicked off to a relatively decent number in Live+7 Day ratings, bringing in 8.6 million total viewers. (It has since allegedly grown that number even further.) I was happy to see it grew the live audience in Week 2, and this past week NBC ultimately ordered extra scripts, which means the first season show should go longer than was originally projected. So what’s the problem?

The freshman drama is only doing OK overall. In terms of Live+ Same Day ratings, the show dropped the last two successive weeks. Then, there’s a fact that it doesn’t fare even close to as well as some of NBC’s more established fare.

Let’s take The Voice, for example. I bring up The Voice even though it is one of the best reality competition series and not a scripted drama because it acts as the lead-in to Line of Fire right now. The Voice actually did fewer viewers than Fire during its premiere, but it also skewed younger. It landed around a .40 share in the advertising demo during its premiere, which is quite a bit better than the .17 ratings demo that Line of Fire did.

This becomes even more important when you have a little context. First, skewing younger means you can sell better ads. Secondly, remember Brilliant Minds? The Zachary Quinto medical drama was only doing a .2 share in the 18-49 demographic by the time its second season rolled around. You know what happened in its second season? The show got canceled.

Peter Krause’s got a great TV track record, hopping from shows like Sports Night to Six Feet Under to Parenthood and 9-1-1. However, let’s not forget there were a few duds in there like The Catch. (Which OK made it two seasons but no one talks about it ever.)

NBC’s said the numbers of younger folk watching the newcomer show has increased since the premiere. In a lot of ways the new show has also compared favorably to its Brilliant Minds predecessor, so again, I’m not completely writing off Line of Fire yet. I’ll be watching, as I love the family dinners (which again, remind me of Blue Bloods in format) and the sharp dialogue between the siblings and parents quite a bit already. There’s still plenty of time, too, before NBC makes a spring decision on some of its on the bubble shows. I just am hoping this one won’t be in the… line of fire… when cancelation season comes around.

Sprouse proved he was Palvin's biggest fan, cheering her on as she stepped out in a baby-pink lace dress during Megan Moroney's performance of "Am I Okay?"

"Ninety percent of the time right now, it's like having a baby pet monkey," he teased on his Wildmen podcast in September. "It is having a pet monkey because she is chirping and making noises and pooping and farting and burping and hiccuping. It's like having a really poopy little animal."

And he was so thrilled to be a girl dad. As he put it, "I did not expect to like this as much as I do, dressing her up in little fits, dude. She's so cute."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If there’s one thing I know about Robert Pattinson, it’s that he’s going to fully transform for whatever part he’s playing. Sometimes that’s through his voice. Other times it’s his entire look. Now, as we approach the release of Dune: Part Three on the 2026 movie schedule, he’s revealed the funny request he had for his character transformation, and it’s very on brand.

With the exception of Dune: Part Three, obviously, I’ve seen every movie Pattinson has released this year. While looks essentially like himself in each, his voice is radically different from performance to performance – he’s British in The Drama, American in The Odyssey and doing an impeccable impression of Chris Hansen in Primetime. This highlights his tendency to really go for it with his performances, lean into the transformations and make some odd and bold choices. He’s about to do that in the new Dune movie too, which is clear in the trailer, but it’s also obvious from the request he had for director Denis Villeneuve, as Pattinson told Empire:

I went into it being like, ‘I want to look like an alien,’ and initially Denis was saying, ‘Well, I think he’s got to fit in with everybody. I think he just looks like you. He’s normal.’ I was a little bit disappointed.

For context, Pattinson plays Scytale in Dune: Part Three. He’s an assassin who is also described as a “shape-shifting ‘Face Dancer’.” The story also notes that his character is from the “genetic-meddling Bene Tleilax people.” That sounds quite alien-like to me, and that’s what the actor wanted. So, it makes sense for both this book-to-screen adaptation in general as well as the actor’s clear adoration for an unexpected makeover.

At first, as he said, he wasn’t going to get that, though. While Dune is a big sci-fi epic, a lot of the cast really didn’t have to change much about their physical appearances to play their characters. However, big transformations have happened; just take a bald Austin Butler in Dune: Part Two as an example. And eventually, Denis Villeneuve realized Pattinson needed a dramatic change in his look too, as the Twilight actor recalled:

It wasn’t even that far before I started shooting; he sent me an email saying, ‘I’ve had this idea of a look.’ And I’m like, ‘Okay! This is very much not like a normal guy at all.’

As you can see in the image above, The Batman star is rocking a very short bleach-blonde haircut and no eyebrows. It is very different from his day-to-day look, and it is quite “alien” like. Explaining why he wanted this dramatically different look, the actor said:

It’s like he’s grown in a lab. There’s a little element of a baby about him, which I really, really liked.

While we’ve seen Robert Pattinson go bleach blonde before – he did it in the film Good Time – this new look is so different from anything we’ve seen him go for. However, that’s what’s so on-brand about it. The man loves a big and bold choice, and I love that he requested this one for Dune: Part Three.

Now, to see him in action as Scytale, you can catch Dune: Part Three in theaters on December 18.

#163. Kylie Jenner Makes Surprise Victoria's Secret Fashion Show Debut

Kyle Jenner sparkled at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show during her surprise appearance in the coveted $50 million fantasy bra, with boyfriend Timothée Chalamet supporting her from his seat.

After all, the Kylie Cosmetics founder made her Victoria's Secret Fashion Show debut on Oct. 18 with a surprise appearance in the coveted $50 million Fantasy Bra as boyfriend Timothée Chalamet and mom Kris Jenner supported her from the audience.

Jenner—the first non-Victoria's Secret model to wear the bra—stepped out in showstopping white angel wings and the diamond-encrusted piece, featuring a fringe of jewels hanging from the band. But the pièce de résistance was the 75.54-carat $22 million diamond at the bra's center.

She completed the look with sparkling panties peeking out from the sheer mini skirt as she walked to Jade Thirlwall's "Angel of my Dreams."

As the 29-year-old showed off the Fantasy Bra—which returned after Ella Hosk last wore it in 2018—Chalamet and Kris, along with her boyfriend Corey Gamble, cheered Jenner on from their seats at Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, Calif.

Jacob & Co. Jewelry shared a glimpse into the making of the bra, valued at $50 million, making it the most valuable Fantasy Bra ever.

“When Victoria's Secret asked us to reimagine one of its most iconic creations, it started with a single question: what if there was no fabric at all?” the company behind the bra wrote on Instagram after the show. “What began as a pencil sketch became a masterpiece of jewelry engineering.”

“Crafted from 3,218 individually designed components, the creation moves with the body like lingerie, combining the brilliance of high jewelry with the fluidity of fashion,” the statement continued. "More than 1,000 hours to create. 15 artisans. 4,410 natural diamonds.”

To bring the idea to life, the company leaned into their shared identity with the lingerie brand.

“Two icons, one shared belief,” Jacob & Co. Jewelry concluded, “the true spectacle should spark joy, inspire confidence and stir emotion.”
