When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Crystal Lake has many admirable qualities, including how it makes you feel like you've been transported right back into the world of Friday the 13th and Jason Voorhees.

Jason is the most well-known villain of this popular horror movie franchise, but it all started with Mother Voorhees. Crystal Lake gives the underrated villain her proper respect.

Linda Cardellini gives one of her best performances in Crystal Lake and makes a compelling case for Pamela being the best thing about the Friday the 13th franchise.

It’s a performance deserving of award attention.

Warning: Crystal Lake spoilers are ahead. Proceed with caution.

A great villain should make you feel like their motives are justified. You should care about them, and in some ways, want them to succeed in their evil plans. I found myself at times rooting for Pamela. Yeah, she was killing people, but didn’t they deserve it a little? The teens alone are kind of nerve testers.

Pamela wouldn’t be as sympathetic if she wasn’t played by someone like Linda Cardellini, who could give the character the depth and empathy she needs to carry a whole series. It’s not often that shows or movies show the perspective of the serial killer. But it’s a story technique that I always admire and appreciate.

You’re not supposed to root for the bad guys, but a great performance and writing can make you change your position on some very evil doers. Pamela is not guilty in my heart. In the crimes she committed, which are many, she is very guilty, though. In my heart, very innocent.

Pamela could be very sympathetic at one moment, and then terrifying the next. She switched between the two modes quite often. Additionally, even when she’s at her most motherly, there is a sinister layer. I would find myself really liking Pamela and then scared of what she might do. I was never comfortable. Crystal Lake and Linda Cardellini kept me on the edge.

A captivating villain should not be predictable. Half the terror and horror in these bad guys is that they don’t follow a set of rules or norms. You fear them because you may understand them, but you can’t predict what they will do. They’re governed more by their emotions and rage than most people.

This makes them deadly but hard to stop watching.

Crystal Lake is such a must-watch horror series that you can watch with a Peacock subscription because it explores a character very important to the franchise but often overlooked and sometimes forgotten. Many didn’t even remember that Pamela was the murderer in the first movie. It was a major iconic pop culture twist that often got erased because Jason became so much the face of the movies.

In telling Pamela’s story, we also learn more about Jason and what turned the sweet boy into this undefeatable monster. Crystal Lake adds layers to Jason and Pamela. I think the decisions, though a bit wacky at times, fit with the idea of Jason.

It gave me a great understanding of Pamela, Jason, and the ridiculous nature of the franchise, but that’s part of the charm.

Spent most of my life in various parts of Illinois, including attending college in Evanston. I have been a life long lover of pop culture, especially television, turned that passion into writing about all things entertainment related. When I'm not writing about pop culture, I can be found channeling Gordon Ramsay by kicking people out the kitchen.

#165. See Gigi Hadid & More on Victoria's Secret Fashion Show 2026 Runway

Gigi Hadid, Barbara Palvin, Adriana Lima, Alessandra Ambrosio, Candice Swanepoel and more walked the runway during the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show. See all the models in their looks.

The 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show kicked off with a high-flying start on Oct. 18, with Bella Hadid opening the festivities in spectacular style. (Click here to see all the celebrity guests on the pink carpet.)

The show was also blessed with the presence of many Victoria's Secret Angels—including Gigi Hadid, Adriana Lima, Alessandra Ambrosio, Candice Swanepoel and Barbara Palvin, who sashayed down the runway just one month after giving birth to her and husband Dylan Sprouse's first baby.

But what made this year's Victoria's Secret show so extra heavenly was the return of the lingerie label's iconic Fantasy Bra after an eight-year absence. Designed by Jacob & Co. jeweler Jacob Arabo, the latest piece boasted a $50 million worth of diamonds—including a centerpiece costing $22 million alone—for Kylie Jenner to wear in her VS Fashion Show debut.

“I wanted to create the most expensive Fantasy Bra ever made, but value alone was never enough," Arabo shared in a statement before the show. “For me, it had to be about the diamonds, the light, and the movement."

And the task of modeling the multi-million bustier is no small feat. Ask Elsa Hosk, who had the honor of donning the 2018 Fantasy Bra.

To the delight of hardcore SNL fans and comedy nerds everywhere, we got an SNL and SNL UK crossover last night. During the cold opener, James Austin Johnson was brought on to do his fantastic impression of President Donald Trump, and not surprisingly, he crushed on the other side of the pond too. Johnson peppered his trademark rambling with plenty of UK references and had the cast members sharing the scenes with him trying to fight off laughter as he ripped on them for not having anyone in the cast that could play the President.

The video of Austin’s appearance has already been watched more than a million times on YouTube, which is a huge number for the first day of an SNL UK clip. The dozens of comments I looked through were all extremely positive too and about equally split between fans praising the comedian’s impression and fans hyping up the fact that we finally got a collaboration. I wholeheartedly agree with both takes and now my brain is going a mile a minute thinking of all the collaborations I want to see. Specifically, it’s thinking of one collaboration I want to see.

Before I get into where I hope this heads, you can check out the full video of Johnson’s impression below…

There’s obviously a whole host of beloved SNL characters I’d love to see on the UK version, as well as some outrageous British weirdness that I’d love to see on the flagship version, but to me, there’s a pretty clear collaboration that we need and that would make a ton of sense. We desperately need a Weekend Update swap.

Some random SNL UK sketches have gone viral and there’s been a lot of positivity around the cast, but I think the most consistently buzzy thing about SNL UK, at least from our perspective in the United States, has been the spinoff’s take on Weekend Update. Co-anchors Paddy Young and Ania Magliano have developed a really nice chemistry and read the fake news without pulling a single punch. At least a joke or two of theirs gets shared widely on social media after every episode.

It would be fun to expose Young and Magliano to a wider audience in the United States, and it would be fun to bring Michael Che and Colin Jost over to SNL UK as a delightful surprise for fans. They’ve, of course, been hosting the US version for over a decade now and are widely considered to be among the best to ever do it. Just as the live audience lost their minds when they saw James Austin Johnson’s Trump, I’d have to imagine they would be so fired up to see Jost and Che.

Beyond just the novelty, however, it would be nice to see both duos get out of their comfort zone and work on jokes for a new audience. I’m sure Che and Jost would have a field day coming up with some wild UK-based segments and topics of conversation, and it would be fun for everyone to see Young and Magliano go for the throat with some jokes that would likely feel edgier and more aggressive than what the US audience normally gets to see.

I have no idea if James Austin Johnson’s guest appearance is a sign that we’re about to get a lot more crossovers or if it’ll go down as a one-off bit of fun. We've gotten SNL stars as hosts before, but this felt like a more direct shared universe situation. Personally, I’d like to see this sorta thing happen a lot more often, and if we’re going to go there, I really need to see this Weekend Update swap.

#167. Barbara Palvin Returns to Victoria's Secret Runway After Giving Birth

Supermodel Barbara Palvin made an epic return to the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show runway on Oct. 18 a little over one month after giving birth to her and Dylan Sprouse’s first baby.

Barbara Palvin is taking super to another level.

Indeed, just over one month after giving birth to her and Dylan Sprouse's first baby, the supermodel made an angelic return to the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show.

While strutting on the runway Oct. 18, the 33-year-old—who is six weeks post-partum—made sure to spread her wings like only she can, wearing a baby pink lacy baby doll as Megan Moroney sang "Am I Okay?" To top off her look, she completed her racy ensemble with large gold hoop earrings.

Meanwhile, Sprouse was seen standing up in the crowd cheering on his wife.

But this wouldn’t be the first time that Palvin completed a flawless catwalk after a major life circumstance. In fact, her husband previously revealed that Palvin powered through her walk at the 2025 show just weeks after breaking her one of her feet.

“She's got a foot that's recovering, which is very funny to me,” Sprouse told E! News last October at the event while on the pink carpet.  “The adrenaline's gonna kick on and she's gonna walk just fine, but I am nervous at the same time for her.”

And though the Suite Life star may have had nerves on his wife’s behalf, she’s always cool as a cucumber.

“She's very nonchalant about everything,” he noted at the time. “She’s just like, ‘Ah, well, today's the day.’ I'm like, ‘But you've trained for months. Don't you get stage fright?’”

Not to mention, Palvin also underwent surgery for endometriosis that summer.

"I had the surgery in June and it's like day and night," she told E! News backstage ahead of the show at the time. "The difference is so crazy. Obviously, it's something that's still very under-researched."

But all in all, she was more than happy to have Sprouse by her side.

"Dylan's been extremely supportive," she explained, "and helped me through the whole recovery process and everything."

It’s a sentiment he also expressed right before her return this year.

“Proud of my missus, jumping right into the vs fashion show post birth,” he wrote in an Oct. 16 Instagram Story post featuring a photo of Palvin and their baby. “Built different. I don’t know where you find the energy from but damn!”

I’ve been (not so) patiently waiting for VisionQuest since we last left Westview, and I’m so glad it’s finally come to the 2026 TV schedule. One thing I can’t stop thinking about whenever I see Vision in his White Vision appearance is the work that goes into making him look like that. Yes, the Vision makeup is “a pain in the ass,” but Paul Bettany has a great (and sassy) take on it.

The 55 year-old actor has been promoting the new Marvel series, and the topic of makeup came up when he spoke with ComicBook about his BTS experiences. Bettany keeps being drawn back to the MCU, and deaths have not been able to keep his character from returning. In fact, the biggest change for the actor is the makeup. When asked if the maroon or white makeup was easier to remove, his response was classic Bettany:

They're equally tricky to get off, and it's a pain in the ass. But I get paid very well. I hate hearing actors moaning about how hard something was. It's a very uncomfortable costume and makeup that I then get financially remunerated for.

There may be some debate about if Vision is the weakest Avenger, but his makeup is certainly the strongest. Personally, his return has been one of the things I’ve been most excited about with Marvel, and Bettany has already wowed critics with his performance in VisionQuest. In just two episodes, we’ve seen the actor pull back new layers to the character, and that includes his time in Westview (even if he doesn’t want to talk about that). By the looks of the trailer, Bettany certainly had a time going between the white and maroon makeup.

We don’t know who Vision will choose to embrace at the end of the series, and the actor certainly hasn’t helped make that clearer, but we do know we’ll get to see him as different versions. It’s an interesting visual approach to the metaphoric journey of finding oneself as Vision struggles with the age-old question of, “Who am I?” Though for Bettany part of that comes with sitting through extensive makeup, though when the hope of him staying around came up, Bettany doubled down with a classic response:

They can put me in tights and swing me around by my genitals for many years to come.

While I feel for any of the actors who have to strap into a harness to fly, I do love seeing Bettany in his full Vision aesthetic. Besides, we know the star is willing to go all in (or take it all off) for a role. I think we can all agree that we want to see Vision around the MCU for years to come, especially since we have yet to see a full Maximoff family reunion. (At least we’ve gotten an amazing reunion between Ultron and Vision.)

I have wonder if Bettany’s a little jealous of his on-screen family’s lack of makeup. Both Elizabeth Olsen and Joe Locke got to don epic costumes as the Scarlet Witch and Wiccan without the hours in the makeup chair. However, nothing is quite as iconic as Bettany’s cheeky approach, and honestly it makes the character even better.

If a full reunion is in the cards for VisionQuest is anyone’s guess. For now, you can check out Bettany’s different makeup looks with a Disney+ subscription and hopefully get that visual the actor supplied out of your mind.

#169. That's It, I've Finally Reached My Breaking Point With Sherlock Holmes Adaptations

That’s it. I’ve had enough. Stop with the Sherlock Holmes adaptations. Earlier this year, Enola Holmes 3 dropped on the 2026 movie schedule, and after watching about a third of it with my Netflix subscription, I got bored, and I still haven't finished it. Then came news that Roku would be producing a show called Scarlett Holmes, starring Lucy Hale as the titular character. That is on top of the news that Sky TV is producing The Death of Sherlock Holmes and Harry King Television is making an adult-oriented animated show about the legendary literary detective. There is no end to the book-to-screen adaptations of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s character. I’ve had it.

I don’t know why Scarlett Holmes set me off, but perhaps it’s the logline given by Roku in their press announcement:

Scarlett Holmes has inherited her family’s legendary powers of observation, but instead of solving crimes, she takes on mysteries of love, dating, and relationships. In each episode, Scarlett is joined by her trusty sidekick, “Jane Watson,” as they help clients navigate mixed signals, secret crushes, romantic dilemmas, and everything in between.

So…Holmes is being adapted into a rom-com? I guess, sure, why not? It’s the one genre that hasn’t previously been explored, I suppose. I doubt very much I’ll be watching, and I like rom-coms! And Lucy Hale, for that matter.

It’s the latest in a seemingly endless number of adaptations in the last couple of decades. Obviously, there are the Guy Ritchie movies starring Robert Downey Jr. as Sherlock. There is also the amazing TV adaptation starring Benedict Cumberbatch as the mercurial detective. There is the aforementioned Enola Holmes, and its sequels, with Millie Bobby Brown as Mycroft and Sherlock's sister. Then there is CBS’s Elementary, which ran for seven seasons. Don’t forget about the current CBS show Watson, a modern take on Dr. Watson from the Doyle stories.

Oh, and there's Sherlock & Daughter on The CW last year, and Young Sherlock, which hit the 2026 TV schedule earlier this year, and you can watch with a Prime subscription. Don’t forget the absolutely terrible parody film Holmes & Watson starring Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly from a few years ago. How many is that? I lost count.

I love Sherlock Holmes. I’ve read all the stories, and I’ve seen most of these adaptations. BBC’s Sherlock with Cumberbatch and Martin Freeman is my favorite, though I do have a soft spot for Jonny Lee Miller and Lucy Liu as Holmes and Watson in Elementary. I liked the first Enola Holmes and saw it as a fresh take on the old idea, but now Hollywood is taking it to the extreme. Enough is enough, already. If they’re not going to bring back Cumberbatch and Freeman, I’m throwing in the towel.

This doesn’t have to be forever, but do we really need like a dozen adaptations in the works at all times? Let’s let Sherlock get some well-deserved rest and get back to him down the road, when we can actually be hungry for a new adaptation.

These days Practical Magic is a spooky season classic, but did you know that when the original movie came out, it flopped? It disappointed at the box office and was slammed by critics. It's, of course, since been embraced by audiences, and a sequel was just part of the 2026 movie schedule. Now, Sandra Bullock has taken some time to celebrate the movie’s ongoing importance and take shots at its critical reception.

The first Practical Magic movie hit theaters this weekend back in 1998. Here’s how Bullock remembered the witchy comedy on its anniversary:

28 years ago today, the first Practical Magic premiered. It was quite polarizing, with critics saying it had too many women, a tone that couldn’t quite find its footing, and was somehow too scary for children and too childish for adults. But what it was, at its heart, was a story about how we choose to love courageously, even in the face of heartbreak.

Practical Magic holds a quite low critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes. Washington Post’s Eve Zibart, for example, characterized it as “just a TV-ready mix of camp and curdle” at the time. Iconic critic Roger Ebert was the one who called it “too scary for children and too childish for adults,” and NY Times’s Janet Maslin described it as “nothing but a guilty pleasure”. The "too many women" comment is especially wild when you think about it.

The movie also made $94 million against a reported production budget of around $75 million. As Sandra Bullock pointed out in her new post on Instagram, despite its commercial reception, Practical Magic has remained a very special movie to its fans. As she added:

Somewhere along the way, it found its audience and became something far greater than any of us could have imagined. Now, 28 years later, there’s another chapter to the story with Practical Magic 2. This new chapter is still full of women, maybe a little too scary for children, and just the right amount of childish for adults.

It took a long time for Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman to reunite for the sequel, but thanks to the movie becoming beloved over time, they made Practical Magic 2. The sequel also earned a similar score on RT (36%), but audiences who saw it were very happy to come back to it and gave it a lot of praise. Bullock also said this as she celebrated the anniversary:

As Alice Hoffman wrote, ‘My darling girl, when are you going to realize that being normal is not necessarily a virtue? It rather denotes a lack of courage.’

What an apt quote for Practical Magic from the source material itself! The new movie allowed Bullock and Kidman to continue the story with Sally and Gilly Owens as middle-aged women – something we don’t see too often in big studio films. Practical Magic 2 opened at No. 1 at the box office and made $104.6 million worldwide. It wasn’t a stunning success either, but fans definitely showed up for this one. I expect once those with an HBO Max subscription can check it out, it’ll only soar higher.

Bullock’s message about the Practical Magic movies led Julianne Hough to write “All time favorite forever and always,” Olivia Munn posted a comment that said “It was, is and will always be a love letter to sisters and friends,” and so many others left messages about how much this movie means to them. Many cited watching the films with their own sisters and making powerful memories with them and Practical Magic.

They may not be critically acclaimed blockbusters, but they’re treasured by so many people, and doesn’t that mean more?

This CBS newbie has some very direct thoughts.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss has faced a considerable amount of backlash since she was hired roughly a year ago, and that criticism arguably expanded this past summer. During those months, Weiss initiated an overhaul of 60 Minutes, which saw several veteran anchors and correspondents fired. That paired with accusations of editorial bias have landed Weiss in hot water. Now, one of the previously mentioned show’s newest on-air talents is now speaking out and providing some blunt advice for his colleagues amid the blowback.

Sir Trevor Phillips – a veteran British broadcaster – was one of several people hired by Weiss ahead of 60 Minutes' return to the 2026 TV schedule for its 59th season. Phillips also serves as CBS’ senior global affairs correspondent and, at this point, he’s received critiques for joining Weiss and co. This past week, Phillips reportedly took part in a meeting of the company’s London bureau. It was during that discussion that Phillips apparently dropped an f-bomb when suggesting what his colleagues should say to the brand’s critics:

Why don’t you just fuck off and let us do our jobs?

According to The Guardian, the sentiment was shared in the midst of a heated conversation, which saw foreign editor Shayndi Raice scold several unidentified employees. Raice took issue with some staffers likening editorial oversight to “interference” and asserted that any disobedience towards editors would result in “legal grounds for firing.” Per the news outlet, Phillips defended Raice’s rationale and expressed his surprise that “that any of this actually has to be said.” Phillips also acknowledged the backlash he’s received for joining CBS:

I could spend the next hour telling you the number of people when it was announced that I was coming here, the number of people who told me for all of the reasons you just explained, why this is the end of my career and how I was going to destroy everything that I’ve ever created, and all of that bollocks.

Phillips joined the company in June 2026 after leaving Sky News, where he hosted his own morning show. That announcement came on the heels of series alums correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi, Scott Pelley and Cecilia Vega being fired along with others like former EP Tanya Simon and Draggan Mihailovich. Pelley, who was reportedly fired after accusing Bari Weiss of “murdering” the show, has been particularly vocal. He opined that the Eye Network as a whole was in need of some “adult supervision.”

How’s Bari Weiss Feeling Amid Paramount’s Merger? She Shared A Message With CBS News Staffers

Nevertheless, as he did during that recent meeting, Phillips has fought back against backlash. He mostly notably defended Weiss during an interview conducted over the summer and said Weiss and her team had a “huge tanker of a network news organisation to turn around”. On top of that, when discussing Weiss more directly, he opined that “the great thing about her is that she’s one of those people who will either change the world or crash and burn.” On that note, the company’s news offerings – like 60 and CBS Mornings – have seen gains and losses as of late.

Although Bari Weiss has had her share of defenders, backlash against her reported editorial methods ensue, and rumors of staffers’ frustrations with her are still in the ether as well. Now that she’s also not going to be involved with CNN following the Paramount/Warner Bros. merger, the Free Press figurehead will theoretically continue to devote the bulk of her time to CBS News. What those efforts might yield is unclear but, in the meantime, it seems Sir Trevor Phillips is firmly supporting both her and their co-workers.

At this point, the general public has come to expect a certain kind of animation style from upcoming Disney movies, which is based in computer animation. While the House of Mouse never ceases to put a smile on my face with each new release even to this day, I can’t help but feel nostalgic for the 2D animation style I grew up with. If you feel the same way, I must point you in the direction of a Lilo & Stitch short hitting theaters this fall, as it beautifully uses that classic style.

CinemaBlend had a chance to visit Walt Disney Animation Studios in Burbank, CA in September, and we were surprised with a screening of Lilo & Scratch. It’s a short film that will play before the studio’s next movie, Hexed. And, y’all need to see it! When seeing a 2D animated Disney movie on the big screen again, I felt like I was transported to my childhood. Here’s the poster:

The short film utilizes the 2D animation style of the original 2002 movie to tell a cute and hilarious little story of a chaotic pink cat (who may have connections to Stitch) joining the Pelekai home. It’s always fun to see Stitch freak out at stuff, and it’s such a good time watching him square off against the tiny but powerful Scratch. And, yes, Chris Sanders reprises Stitch, with live-action Lilo & Stitch actress Maia Kealoha stepping into the recording booth to voice Lilo.

During CB's visit at Walt Disney Animation, co-directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Malcon Pierce told us that the studio created a new pipeline that would combined the use of hand-drawn animation with their modern computer-based animation models to make the short happen. What I found exceptionally cool is that they even dug up some of the watercolor backgrounds from the original movie to serve as the backdrops for this new production. After we saw the production, Veerasunthorn told us this about creating the pipeline:

The pipeline came from so many people in the studio who wanted to work on it, and they were like, ‘Would it be this or would it be that?’ And we were like, ‘What if it's all of it?’ If you wanna work on this short film, you can. And, we created the pipeline to accommodate all of that. It's super fun.

I love to hear about Disney animators coming together to bring Lilo & Stitch to life as we remember it. And this isn't the first time in recent years that 2D animation has been utilized by the studio. A few years ago, Disney’s Wish was heavily influenced by hand-drawn animation along with the short Once Upon A Studio, which was made in celebration of the company’s 100-year anniversary.

So, of course, I had to pose the question: Could Disney make a feature film with this pipeline? Jason Hand, who is co-director on Hexed and previously co-helmed Moana 2, had this to say:

I mean, we use 2D in our film [Hexed]. The opening is a hand drawn part. So, I think whatever tells the story best, I'm up for.

How cool is it that 2D animation has a larger presence in Walt Disney Animation again? Not only that, but the mere existence of Lilo & Scratch also harkens back to the good old days of seeing shorts before Disney movies. That's something that hasn’t happened since Encanto back in 2021.

To put it simply, anyone who grew up with Disney flicks during the early aughts, should check out Lilo & Scratch along with Hexed, when the latter hits the 2026 movie schedule on November 25. I not only hope fans enjoy the short but that it also starts a new wave of 2D-animated productions.

I’ve been watching Dancing with the Stars on and off for almost all of my life, and for decades I’ve known one thing to be true: Carrie Ann Inaba will call out a lift when it’s not allowed. However, oftentimes, when she does this, it causes quite the commotion online. That happened in a big way when the Super Bowl episode of Season 35 aired on the 2026 TV schedule, and she aggressively called out a lift included in Jenna Johnson and Harry Shum Jr.’s dance.

So, as I’ve witnessed a passionate and wild discourse play out online, I decided to look up what exactly the lift rules are on Dancing with the Stars.

While Super Bowl Night sparked lots of conversations online that ranged from Guillermo’s elimination to Julia Stiles' Save the Last Dance tribute, the lift debacle has been the main thing I’ve been thinking about. That’s because while I know Carrie Ann is a stickler about lifts, I wasn’t expecting her to end her very critical comments with:

A lift is, I just need to say it, ‘Any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor with the assistance of their partner.’ Yeah, lift.

Now, when Carrie Ann first said there was a lift, Jenna Johnson responded in shock by saying, “A lift?” and you can see that play out by watching the episode with a Disney+ subscription. Then, when the pro got up to the skybox, she explained that the comment shocked her because she thought the rule was that “if you lifted your partner,” and it was the troupe who lifted Harry, not her.

Overall, it was an awkward situation, and it’s left me with questions about what exactly the rules are when it comes to lifts.

As I mentioned, this is not the first time Carrie Ann Inaba’s strict feelings about lifts and her judging in general have caused intense discourse. So, yes, she has addressed the rules and how she applies them to the show multiple times before. For example, in 2015, she wrote a blog for Parade that stated:

The producers have had this rule in place since the first season. I know it upsets people but it is a rule. I think there is some confusion on what a lift is: according to the National Dance Council of America Rule Book, ‘A lift is any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner.’

I double-checked the National Dance Council of America Rule Book as well, and that definition (which is also the one she read while critiquing Harry and Jenna) is still the exact one that’s used today. However, this rule does not apply to all dances. Sometimes lifts are allowed, and other times they are not, as Inaba explained:

They can’t do lifts in any of the standard dances or the Latin dances, but lifts are allowed in Jazz, Contemporary, Charleston, Salsa, Argentine Tango and the non-ballroom dances. Just to clarify, I do not get any joy in docking a point for breaking a rule. Rules are rules and I do my best to enforce them.

So, to make it clearer, lifts are not allowed in styles like:

However, as Inaba wrote, they are allowed in styles like:

Now you know why she’ll compliment lifts sometimes and call them out other times. It also explains why she had the reaction she did to Harry and Jenna’s dance.

So, as we move forward with this season of Dancing with the Stars, keep this rule in mind, because it explains why Carrie Ann Inaba reacts the way she does to lifts. Now, with all that explained and out of the way, you can catch new episodes of DWTS every Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET on ABC or Disney+.

She really was the perfect choice for Nikki.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Curry Barker’s successful summer flick, Obsession, became a word-of-mouth sensation that left many horror fans themselves obsessed. One major element that critics all agree makes the film memorable is its lead, Inde Navarette, who gives a truly nightmare-inducing performance scene after scene. If you want to know how dedicated Navarette was to giving audiences chills (and her director), the talented actress said she refused to rehearse one surprising scene.

Bear’s wish for Nikki to love him more than anyone goes back to the adage, “Be careful what you wish for.” Through Nikki’s supernatural transformation, Navarette brought maniacal terror to each spine-chilling scene. None of those moments were done without rehearsal, except apparently for one scene. During an episode of The Hollywood Reporter’s Awards Chatter podcast, Navarette recalled director Curry Barker being shocked when she said she wouldn't practice a key moment:

We shot when they’re making out on Bear’s bed and she goes, ‘What the—?!’ and then she shoots backwards. That was our first day. And that was a pretty big task. Before going in, I told Curry, ‘I’m really sorry, but I’m not going to show you any of the freakouts in rehearsal.’ And I think I saw him die, because… it’s very important for the character. I felt like if I gave it away too early, it wasn’t going to be as authentic as I needed it to be… I really wanted to keep that safe before it needed to come out in order to play it true.

The Critic’s Choice Super Award winner took a bold stance by not rehearsing that bed scene, but her rationale made sense. After all, what makes Nikki’s freakouts so horrifying to watch are how spontaneous they are. So, naturally, the versatile lead wanted to save the freaky Nikki scenes for when the cameras rolled to make it a genuine performance. I mean, I personally didn’t see it coming whenever the Nikki would make an appearance and freak out after her makeout session with Bear. So, I’d say a job well done.

It may be typical for actresses to leave it to rehearsal to see what works and what doesn’t. But, for Navrette, she needed to let her instincts take over on set, compared to letting everyone see what she was going to do first. She explained:

And so we’re in the first day, I know Curry’s nervous, I know that I’m really being a dick by saying ‘I’m not going to show you anything.’ But I mean, he’ll even say now that it was a weight lifted off of his shoulders when we did that first freakout, because he was like, ‘Oh my God, OK, she can do it! She just needs privacy with these things.’

While we don't need any directors to "die" here, Navarette created quite an impressive strategy to avoid revealing Nikki’s haunting nature until "action" was heard. It clearly worked, as it apparently brought chills to the YouTuber and box-office-smashing director. I can imagine that in those unexpected frantic moments, the indie filmmaker knew he made the right call by casting Navarette for his horror flick.

Not only did Inde Navarette go method actress in keeping Nikki’s freakouts a secret until filming, but she also emotionally distanced herself from her co-workers to focus on her performance instead of worrying about offending anyone through her Nikki portrayal. With all of the hard work and effort that the X-Men star brought into Obsession, I wouldn’t be surprised if we saw her name during this year’s awards season.

What Navaratte's behind-the-scenes story shows is that she's not just committed to her craft, but she's also willing to advocate for herself when it's necessary. Considering that, I have a feeling we're going to be watching this true talent on screen for some time. If you haven’t had a taste of Nikki under the One Wish Willow, Obsession is streaming now with a Peacock subscription.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

I'm still not over Jessie's Toy Story 5 arc.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

One core memory I’ll always have from this year is watching Toy Story 5 in theaters and being moved by Jessie returning to her tire swing. Before I saw it, I thought I knew what was going to happen in the third-act scene, but Pixar caught me off guard with what happened instead. However, I just found out my initial intuition about Jessie was actually going to happen before the filmmakers decided to pivot...and man, am I happy they went in this different direction.

As it turns out, in the original iteration of Toy Story 5, Jessie was going to meet an elderly Emily at the end of the movie. Co-writer Kenna Harris revealed the BTS detail while attending the VIEW Conference in Torino, Italy, on Friday (via Variety).

The change was one of numerous alterations she helped make to Toy Story 5 that ultimately made it one of the best projects on the 2026 movie schedule. At one point, Pixar decided to halt production on the film for two weeks to rework some of it. Harris recalled that “act one was not working” at first, and the stakes of losing playtime felt “too soft”. The Toy Story 5 rewrite led Harris and Andrew Stanton (who also directed the movie) to make several breakthroughs, such as the importance of Blaze to the storyline, for example.

While Jessie reuniting with Emily sounds all kinds of emotional and full circle, the filmmakers thought it resolved Jessie’s inner turmoil too conveniently. So, they ended up going with the teary-eyed resolution we can now see in the movie.

I remember that before sitting down to watch Toy Story 5 over the summer, I was sure the movie was teasing a reconciliation between Jessie and Emily many years later. One thing that seemed to really point in that direction is Taylor Swift’s song “I Knew It, I Knew You”, which was released before the film.

So, I was taken aback when something else happened. While Jessie and Bullseye are at the old tire swing where she used to play with Emily, she finds a lunch box under the soil where she makes a discovery. Emily ended up naming her own daughter after Jessie.

While I expected Emily to come back into Jessie’s life, I didn't see it happening this way, and it made the instance between the cowgirl and her former kid even more emotional than I anticipated. It would have been an obvious story beat if Jessie and Emily ran into each other, but Jessie finding this time capsule and having the realization that even though she was given away, she was always important to Emily is actually even more powerful. And it makes all the difference for Jessie.

I know I’m far from the only one who was completely moved by Jessie’s arc in Toy Story 5. The cowgirl's backstory has always stuck with me, and there’s something so gratifying about seeing a part of her heal through this unexpected moment with Emily that's more grounded in reality.

You can watch Toy Story 5 and revisit this endearing sequence right now with a Disney+ subscription.

Warning! There are some pretty big spoilers for You Can See Everything in this story. If you haven’t seen the 2026 movie, you might want to stop here. I don’t want to show everything before you see it.

There is a lot to talk about in the new Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim documentary, You Can See Everything. The movie is, in a word, bonkers. That’s a word I used to describe the trailer when I first saw it, and I’m standing by it now that I’ve seen the movie. There are countless scenes in the movie that make you really wonder what the heck is going on with the film’s subject, former Theranos CEO and current jailbird, Elizabeth Holmes. There are just as many with her husband, Billy Evans. It’s one scene in particular that, for me, really sums up a lot of the movie: when Evans takes the bowl of eggs out of Holmes’ hands to scramble them when he sees she’s not doing what he wants.

The scene comes pretty early in the nearly three-hour movie, which has been buzzed about ever since the trailer went viral. Evans and Holmes are cooking in their rented cottage on the beach when Evans wordlessly takes the bowl and starts beating the eggs himself. I actually gasped out loud because it’s a moment that really shows Evans’ controlling nature. No woman I’ve ever dated would put up with that, nor should they, but Holmes acquiesces without any pushback. It’s the first glimpse into Evans’ personality and their relationship, really, but hardly the last.

Fielder notices it and immediately calls the two out for the action. He saw how weird it was, but Holmes is unfazed (something you could say about her for the whole movie). He asks her about it, and she tells him that it’s fine, that Evans doesn’t like the way she beats eggs. Like, what? That is a weirdly specific thing to take umbrage at, and it’s disconcerting, to say the least. It’s not the last time we see Evans try to control everything around him. It's a brilliant bit of filmmaking, too, as the audience immediately understands who Evans is in just that one moment.

I want to be careful here, because I do not believe that Elizabeth Holmes is, or ever has been, a victim. Not in her scam with her company’s medical device, for which she is currently serving time in a Federal prison in Texas, and not in this movie. That said, her husband, who met her after Theranos imploded under the weight of her massive fraud, is equally upsetting here. They are both villains, as I see it.

He is repeatedly shown trying to control things he cannot, most notably in Fielder and Oppenheim’s film. He also does things that are completely outlandish, like the way he asks for money for the movie, or the way he acts at dinner after Holmes was incarcerated and he is joined by the film crew and actress Amanda Seyfried. He has a short fuse and obviously doesn’t like things not being under his thumb, as Holmes seems to be so often, as exemplified by a simple scene of the couple cooking eggs.

It’s been well over a year now since Todd and Julie Chrisley were pardoned by U.S. President Donald Trump after serving prison time for finance-based offenses. At this point, the Chrisleys have seemingly returned to their regular lives, but there’s still a question regarding any outstanding debts they may or may not still have. Todd (57) and Julie (53) themselves have mostly steered away from discussions regarding their finances. Now, however, there are details regarding how much money they still owe the IRS.

Todd and Julie Chrisley reportedly owe $1.5 million in unpaid federal taxes to the Internal Revenue Service. According to Page Six, the IRS filed a federal tax lien in August 2026, and that specifically amounts to $1,571,452. Said lien is specifically composed of two separate unpaid tax assessments aimed at the reality TV stars’ portfolio. One of those assessments is dated for December 5, 2022, while the other is dated for December 11, 2023.

An assessment for the tax period ending with Dec. 31, 2021 shows an unpaid balance of $142,410.72. The other one is marked for the period ending with Dec. 31, 2022, and includes a sum of $1,429,041.89. As of this writing, the Chrisleys have not publicly addressed the public releases of these filings.

The Chrisleys were found guilty of bank fraud, tax evasion and more back in 2022 and were sentenced to years in prison. Julie was initially set to serve seven years at Lexington Medical Center in Kentucky, while Todd would serve 12 years at the since-closed Federal Prison Camp in Florida. As part of those verdicts, the couple was ordered to pay $17.2 million in restitution and were seemingly going to have to sell off assets to cover that. As of 2025, said debts weren’t paid, with the Chrisleys explaining it was put on hold due to their appeals.

Todd Chrisley Just Responded To Rumors His Trump Pardon Was ‘Autopen S–t’

In the first few months after they were pardoned, the Chrisleys touched upon their financial well-being following claims that they’d had money issues during their prison stints. Todd scoffed at the rumors of there being such issues in September 2025, though he also wouldn’t confirm how much money he had at the time. What he and Julie did do, however, was reveal that they’d paid roughly $3 million in legal fees throughout their legal saga.

This latest development involving the pair’s taxes marks the latest setback for them in the past several months. Back in April, Todd Chrisley was ordered to pay $750,000 in restitution to ex-tax creditor Amy Doherty-Heinze. Said payment stems from a lawsuit filed by Doherty-Heinze in 2024, as the former Georgia Department of Revenue employee accused the Chrisleys of launching a smear campaign against her during their tax fraud trial.

All the while, there are still questions regarding when or how the Chrisleys might make their return to reality TV. Todd, Julie and their kids famously headlined USA Network’s Chrisley Knows Best for 10 seasons before it ended amid their legal woes. Several years later, their kids participated in a Lifetime docuseries called The Chrisleys: Back to Reality, which slightly overlapped with Julie and Todd’s release. Earlier this summer, Todd asserted that he still wasn’t ready to return to reality TV due to still searching for the right situation.

It’s unclear as to whether these recently revealed tax situations might impede Todd and Julie Chrisley’s attempts to return to TV on a regular basis. The IRS has also not provided further details on the situation at this time.

I would assume that hearing the name Julie Plec strikes a certain chord of nostalgia and excitement in the heart of every Vampire Diaries fan, especially when it’s tied to a new project. Prime Video has greenlit a new YA tennis drama series called Rally from Plec’s My So-Called production company, as part of her deal with Universal Television. Having watched a number of Plec’s popular works, I’ll give anything with her name on it a chance. However, this announcement means it’s time to finally face an unfortunate truth: Julie Plec is officially getting out of the supernatural game.

I can’t believe I’m saying this, but is Julie Plec taking a hiatus from the supernatural game? She helped shape the genre through the 2010s, creating some of the best teen supernatural dramas to date, like The Vampire Diaries and its spin-offs The Originals and Legacies. However, after the cancellations of Legacies and Vampire Academy, Plec seems eager to test her hand at realistic fictional dramas, creating The Girls On The Bus and the popular Prime adaptation of We Were Liars, which has been renewed for a Season 2.

Now, the announcement of Rally marks four years since Plec invited vampires into her life, and she seems to be quite content exploring this new chapter in her television career. However, she remains firm in the YA genre, as Deadline reports Rally will be set “at a hyper-competitive elite tennis academy” where “ambitious young players discover that the loneliest sport in the world demands sacrificing the very connections that might be the only thing that makes winning worth it.”

Aiding Plec in the series creation is Grand Slam champion and American tennis legend Andre Agassi, as well as Entertainment 360 executive producer Guymon Casady. Casady recently served as executive producer on Apple TV+’s sports comedy Stick, which stars Owen Wilson as a washed-up golf pro turned coach and has Season 2 premiering on the 2026 TV schedule in November. The series idea for Rally is based on Casady’s own experience with his sons navigating “elite tennis academy culture,” detailing the many reasons why this project will be something special:

The inspiration for Rally came from a deeply personal place – watching my kids train and navigate the intense pressure, dedication, and heartbreak of elite junior tennis at the IMG Academy. To build this world alongside a master storyteller like Julie Plec, and to ground it in the unmatched, authentic perspective of a true legend like Andre Agassi, is a remarkable privilege.

I think it’s safe to say Entertainment 360, Universal Television, and Prime Video have assembled an all-star team for Rally. I can’t say I blame Plec for taking a step in this direction either. Sports dramas are peaking in audience interest right now, with the continued success of shows like Ted Lasso and Stick, as well as recent acclaimed movies like Challengers (2024) and Marty Supreme (2025). Plus, shows like Off Campus and Heated Rivalry have taken the world by storm. Romeo Beckham is also set to make his acting debut in the upcoming gay tennis drama Forty Love on the 2026 movie schedule. I only hope the genre isn’t oversaturated by the time Rally is available to stream with a Prime Video subscription.

While Plec may be stepping away from the world of werewolves and super hot blood-sucking brothers, I do have faith that the supernatural world will come calling to her once more. The Vampire Diaries co-creator isn't totally against a reboot, and in the past she has suggested a movie revival might be on the table. Though it (unfortunately) doesn’t seem to be anytime soon. However, when the stars align, maybe we will eventually return to Mystic Falls.

When Dolly Parton died at the age of 80 over the summer, Miley Cyrus lost her “fairy” godmother. The pop star has since publicly paid tribute to the late legend and spoken about what people often got wrong about her. More recently, Cyrus took the stage at the Hollywood Bowl this past Friday night, and she paid her most emotional tribute to Parton yet.

Miley Cyrus’ Hollywood Bowl show is her first big concert in four years. In between playing songs from her new album Bass Persuades and hits like “Party In The U.S.A.”, “The Climb” and “Flowers”, she took a few minutes to remember Parton with a sweet memory that made the show extra special. As she revealed to the crowd of over seventeen thousand, there was a very personal reason for her choosing to bring up the late star at the venue:

I only got to see Dolly Parton live in concert one time in my entire life, and it was here.

Cyrus (as seen in a fan’s Instagram video) sat down on the stage as she went on to recall that night to the audience, saying that if it was up to the "Coat of Many Colors" singer, she’d be “standing right beside her in a matching costume" during Parton's own Bowl show. But Cyrus asked if she could simply sit in her seat and watch the show like everybody else. Parton responded with, “OK, Miley," which Cyrus quipped never really just meant “OK" from her godmother. And then this happened, per Cyrus:

So, I’m sitting in my seat back there where you are, and all of a sudden Dolly enters but I hear ‘Best of Both Worlds’. Yeah, Dolly opened by playing Hannah Montana. But, that’s not just the end of that story. She comes out like a proud aunt, ‘I don’t know if y’all know this, but my goddaughter is Hannah Montana, and she’s actually here tonight, but she’s in her seat. She didn’t want anyone to bug her. She just wanted to watch the show,’ which defeated the entire purpose of the conversation we had just had because absolutely no one was aware I was at the concert until she drew an obnoxious amount of attention to it.

How adorable of a story is that? (And, yes, I dug up the cover from 2011 which you can watch on Instagram, and it’s amazing, obviously). While an 18-year-old Miley Cyrus was a little peeved at the time over Parton bringing attention to her at a show where she just wanted to be another fan, it made for a more emotional reason to talk about Dolly that night. As she continued:

Like so many things Dolly did, that I didn’t understand at the time, sitting here with you all right now, feeling her all around me, knowing that she’s right here beside me everyday, all the time, more than she could be when she was here. I feel her, now more than ever. Knowing that I get to share this story with you all, it makes that night very worth it. This memory is gold to me.

Cyrus’ speech is so genuine and nearly had me in tears as I watched her get choked up about Dolly Parton. It’s so clear how important and beautiful their bond was, and I love that she shared a story that really illustrates that bond on a more realistic and familial level. Like, of course if Dolly was your godmother she would embarrass you on stage! Cyrus ended her speech with these words:

Me and Dolly, we are eternal. Nothing in this life could tear us apart. And I’m gonna see her again. I can’t fucking wait because I miss her. Some of the greatest music that we have today was written, produced and performed by my Aunt Dolly.

If I was at that show, the waterworks would've been flowing. Cyrus then sang “Jolene” for the crowd as she has many times before, but this time it hit different.

There have been a lot of celebrity tributes for Parton, but it’s hard to top this one. It definitely makes me want to curl up and watch their work on Hannah Montana with Emily Osment and co. all over again. Cyrus is set to play the Hollywood Bowl again on Sunday night. There’s also a celebratory special for Dolly Parton hitting the 2026 TV schedule this Wednesday, October 21 on ABC. Needless to say, Dolly, we'll always love you!

Was it really the worst movie of all time?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Out of all the movies that people claim are the worst of all time, one that stands out is Gigli. On the surface, the film was a smart move for both of the stars, Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck, as they would be working with acclaimed Scent of a Woman filmmaker Martin Brest. However, the movie was disastrous, with a ridiculous plot, some offensive dialog, and a pretty silly depiction of the central relationship. Now, Affleck is looking back at the infamous film and his real-life romance that impacted it.

Affleck revealed that Gigli essentially got caught up in the tabloid fodder surrounding his relationship with Jennifer Lopez on the Happy, Sad, Confused podcast. They'd met on the set of the movie, started a relationship, and were already an iconic couple before the project premiered. The actor said of the movie:

It was a function of like, we were so over — we're were so exhausted by and overexposed by this Ben Affleck Jennifer Lopez phenomenon, which itself was a function of being a tabloid story at a time when the tabloids really recognized there were they had a much wider audience than they realized. And so there was this huge proliferation of these magazines, and so it seemed as if, you know, we were shoving ourselves down everyone's throats, and we were wildly overexposed. So it was a lot of negative factors at work.

From 2001 to 2003, the two were everywhere. They were on the cover of magazines, were on red carpets, and Affleck famously starred in Lopez's "Jenny from the Block" music video. The Gone Girl star believes that this overexposure had a negative impact on Gigli. The situation was made worse when the movie in question wasn't very good and was quickly considered to be one of the worst movies ever made. Affleck said that he thinks the extreme negativity was a little outsized, explaining:

[It’s] a movie that didn’t work but not like the worst movie. In fact, [of] all the people that mocked and derided it, I think very few actually saw it

He is right that very few people actually saw it. It was made on a $75.6 million budget, and only grossed about $7.3 million. The amount of criticism they got from this situation only piled on to the negative press they were already getting from being overexposed. The movie by itself likely didn’t tank the relationship, but it certainly didn’t help the situation. Gigli came out in August 2003; by September the duo decided to postpone their wedding due to the amount of media attention, and by January 2004 they were over (at least for the time being).

Gigli may have seemed like a career ender at the time. However, the duo ended up coming out on top. Affleck used the situation as a learning experience and had a lustrous movie career after he decided to start making his own movies, starting with 2007’s Gone Baby Gone.

Lopez ended up focusing more on music and is a bestselling recording artist. The duo even gave their love another shot a few years back, and while they ended up getting divorced in January 2025, they seem to still have a lot of respect for each other. It certainly isn’t a bright spot on their careers, but Gigli may not have actually been the disaster we all thought that it was.

Those curious can revisit Gigli now by renting the film on Amazon. Ben Affleck fans can also check out his latest film Animals, which is currently streaming with a Netflix subscription.

#181. Hear Me Out: I Actually Wouldn't Want Inde Navarrette In An Obsession Sequel

I think we can do without "Freaky Nicky."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Obsession easily stands tall as one of 2026's most buzz-worthy movies and made a star out of Inde Navarrette. Now she's landing roles in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but that doesn't mean she'd be above returning for a sequel. She's signaled a few times that she's down to return, but my hot take is I wouldn't want her involved.

It may seem crazy to say, but hear me out. I loved Navarrette's performance, and all that she brought to the movie to make it a success. The raving about her performance is well-deserved, but that doesn't mean we need to include Nicky in a sequel when the story isn't about her.

Obsession's ending left us with questions about what's next for Nicky after she might be found with two dead people and a gun with her fingerprints all over it. After reading the cast's thoughts about it, I think it's safe to say we can shut the book on that storyline. Yes, Inde Navarette's performance was great, but now that she's no longer Wish Nicky, it's not like her appearing in a sequel would bring back that performance.

I'm of the opinion that the One Wish Willow, and the mythos that surrounds the product, is infinitely more interesting and worthy of anything an Obsession sequel could cover. Once the credits rolled, I found myself with more questions tied to that than anything, so I'd much rather see a follow-up centered on that than Nicky.

I have no interest in seeing a sequel retread the ground of the original Obsession, and it seems as though Inde Navarette is on the same page. Rather than a sequel being a straight-up investigation of the One Wish Willow makers, why not create a franchise that revolves around people using the device to make wishes, and then it goes catastrophically wrong?

Seth Rogen Has Already Seen Obsession Director’s Next Movie, And I’m Shook Over His Big Claims

Is it a ripoff of The Monkey's Paw? Inadvertently, yes, because director Curry Barker was only made aware of the story through The Simpsons' parody of it. That aside, that takes nothing away from my enjoyment of the movie, and I'd be thrilled to see what other ways people could potentially ruin their lives with a bad wish.

I'd also just like to see if everyone's One Wish Willow is a bad experience. Like, sure, it can go wrong for some people, but wouldn't it be funny to see a movie where everything works out for the person in the end? Like, imagine a world in which Bear didn't overdose, and he and Nicky are just in some sick, unhealthy romance that other people just happen to stumble in on. I guess that's still a bad ending, but at least they're both alive at the end. In any case, I would love to see more on the One Wish Willow so we could see how it works out for others.

In the meantime, all we have to reference is Obsession, which is streaming for those with a Peacock subscription. I'll be eager to see how this franchise evolves, and if it ultimately enters the conversation of the original being one of the best horror films out there.

During her child star days, Christy Carlson Romano worked with Shia LaBeouf on Even Stevens as well as one of the best DCOMs, The Even Stevens Movie. Their characters, siblings Ren and Louis Stevens, had a sometimes tense, but mostly loving, bond. Yet the actors' real-life relationship apparently wasn’t so affable. I didn’t expect to wake up and see some tea from Romano about LaBeouf but, as a long-time fan of the show, I’m intrigued.

Romano has long been open about her Disney Channel days, like when she had a big crush on her Cadet Kelly co-star, Shawn Ashmore. But the thoughts she shared with E! News about what it was like working with LaBeouf on Even Stevens were particularly candid. Her description of their dynamic suggests things were a bit rough between them:

It was dysfunctional at best. It was a little competitive at times. He was a very ambitious child. He really needed to become famous because his home life was really complicated.

While Romano said the Holes actor didn’t speak much about his parents while working on the teen sitcom, the actor has spoken openly before about his tough upbringing. His real-life story was paralleled in the film Honey Boy. Said movie, which LaBeouf wrote, shed light on his complicated relationship with his dad while being a child star. (However, LaBeouf also later admitted that his dad's abusive nature was exaggerated to a degree for the movie.)

Even Stevens centers on the Stevens family, with each member being successful in their endeavors except for the sitcom’s horribly misbehaved youngest child and black sheep Louis. The show proved to be a hit, and LaBeouf found big-screen success after the Disney Channel show wrapped its three-season run in 2003. Based on Romano's claims, it appears she’s saying the competitive nature their characters had with each other wasn’t far off from real life:

I think that he needed to be the star of Even Stevens, but it was still our show. They made me much more of a costar character. And it just made sense with his schooling. They needed to be able to use me during times that he would be in school.

I feel for Romano in her disappointment that too much attention was being put on the character of Louis when it was supposed to be on the whole family. It’s also sad to hear that the Kim Possible star felt she was only used when LaBeouf was in school. At the same time, though, LaBeouf's character arguably was (and remains) one of the show's signature elements. So, with that in mind, it's easy to understand the business incentive to capitalize on the eventual Transformers star's performance.

A fun fact about Even Stevens was that the show’s original title was going to be Spivey’s Kid Brother, before it was developed into the show kids enjoyed in the early 2000s. In any case, the series was indeed meant to focus on the youngest sibling of a family. Christy Carlson Romano weighed in on why the show’s initial conceit may have been important to LaBeouf's career as a child star:

Initially it was going to be his show. That's what fueled his ambition, his competitive streak, and it's unfortunate because I did come to understand that he had this complicated relationship with his dad. At the same time, I wanted to be there for him, but I knew that I could never really fully be there for him because we had this work-life imbalance.

It looks like Romano has an understanding of why LaBeouf apparently felt the need to strive hard to play Louis Stevens to mask his home life. The PodCo founder expressed in her memoir how “small and helpless” she felt after overhearing an argument the Indiana Jones actor had with his dad on set.

All in all, it's interesting to get behind-the-scenes details on one of Disney Channel's most beloved shows decades later. If anything it provides more context to the production. As for where Christy Carlson Romano and Shia LaBeouf currently stand, she revealed that hadn't been in touch since reuniting at a 2005 premiere, but she still wishes her on-screen brother the best.

You can watch the sibling rivalry of Ren and Louis by streaming Even Stevens with a Disney+ subscription now. Feel free to also check out Romano’s memoir Once Upon a Trainwreck: The Fall and Rise of a Child Star, available for purchase on Amazon and at your local bookstores.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

The filmmaker isn't mincing words about this.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

James Gunn definitely has no problem setting the record straight when it comes to DC-related rumors. The filmmaker/exec – who runs DC Studios alongside Peter Safran – has consistently taken to social media to field questions from fans regarding the rumor mill. More recently, Gunn and co. have been contending with chatter surrounding upcoming DC movies like Man of Tomorrow and The Batman: Part II. A user recently took to the web to lay out some gossip they’d heard, and Gunn didn’t mince words about “BS” chatter.

One user reached out to Gunn on Threads, where they mentioned three items of speculation. The first is in regard to the status of the recently stalled The Batman: Part II, which alleges that Matt Reeves is stepping away from the film entirely. Another rumor mentioned was an allegation about actress Milly Alcock not playing the DCU’s Supergirl in the long run. And, finally, the third rumor the fan brought up alleged that Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow had a poor test screening, because it allegedly killed off a major character.

The Guardians of the Galaxy helmer took notice of the claims, and shared some honest thoughts. In the process, he not only provided some advice to the user but to other fans as well:

Oh brother. You guys just have to stop listening to BS, and I'm mostly done shooting down rumors as there are so many and I'm not on here much. But all three of these couldn't be more false. I'm showing PETER SAFRAN my first Director's Cut today - he's the first person to see it obviously - and that's a month early!

I’ve found it interesting (and entertaining) to see how Gunn responds to the constant influx of rumors that surround the work he and his colleagues are doing. The filmmaker’s tone can vary, based on the subject. For example, earlier this year, he had no problem dubbing MoT casting rumors “crazy” and, a few months ago, he also debunked rumors about the long-gestating The Brave and the Bold and the Waller TV show. On the other hand, Gunn had a jokier response when discussing the prospect of a Superman director’s cut.

As part of his response, James Gunn clearly poured water on the notion of that MoT test screening, since Safran has only just seen a director’s cut. That aside, there’s also public knowledge regarding the statuses of the Batman sequel and Milly Alcock.

It’s true that Matt Reeves’ latest Batman film has seen its share of starts and stops and, most recently, it was confirmed that filming had been paused due to Reeves dealing with a family matter. This week, it was reported that Steven Soderbergh would oversee principal photography on the remainder of the shoot and would remain in close communication with Reeves throughout. On top of that, Reeves is stressing that he’s “not leaving” the movie and that he would be hands-on again during post-production.

As for Milly Alcock, that aforementioned rumor comes months after Supergirl’s underperformance at the box office. However, it’s already known that Alcock will reprise her role as Zara Zor-El in Man of Tomorrow. The character’s future hasn’t been confirmed beyond the move, but Gunn’s response seems to suggest the notion of Alcock not being the one to play the character is far-fetched.

Chances are that as time goes on, DC rumors will continue to make the rounds and, if history is anything to go off, James Gunn will work to differentiate fact from fiction. I can’t imagine constantly taking to the web to address speculation but, in all honesty, a part of me does appreciate Gunn’s efforts.

Spoilers for the first two episodes of Fire Country’s fifth season are ahead! You can stream them with a Paramount+ subscription.

Bode and CJ’s budding friendship on Fire Country is one of my favorite relationships the show has had, and the new firefighter has only been around for two episodes. To me, it's clear that these two are kindred spirits in a way, and their chemistry together is just delightful. However, while I can’t wait to see their friendship flourish as Fire Country’s shortened season airs on the 2026 TV schedule, I also have one major concern I need to talk about.

From the jump, I found the sparky energy between Bode and CJ very endearing, and so far, I’ve loved seeing them start to bond. It’s also been fun to see the origin of this relationship with the knowledge that Olivia Thirlby’s character is in this for the long haul because she’s the first regular Fire Country has added since it premiered.

Moving forward, I’m excited to see how these two support and help each other. It becomes clear in Episode 2 that CJ has gone through some traumatizing experiences before she made it to Edgewater that she’s haunted by. While Bode’ history isn’t the same, he does have ghosts and demons he’s still dealing with, and he’s very open about his past as a criminal and how he’s grown since then. With all that in mind, I’m excited to see how these two can help each other positively evolve and heal. I also think they’ll work really well together professionally as they develop the volunteer firefighter program.

On top of that, we learn in Episode 2 that CJ’s former co-workers are not good, and it seems like they could be out to get her. I’m sure Bode will passionately help her.

Overall, the groundwork for a lovely (and potentially dramatic) friendship has been laid, and I hope we stay on that trajectory.

Unfortunately, when it comes to relationships between men and women on TV, it’s common to assume that it could easily turn romantic. When it comes to Bode, that’s a fair assumption to make too, because he’s had multiple romantic relationships on the show. Notably, Max Thieriot's character has been in relationships with Gabriela and Audrey, and now he’s with Alona Tal’s Chloe.

Chloe and Bode's relationship is just getting started; however, we haven’t seen them together in Season 5 yet. And I’m a bit worried that he might also develop feelings for CJ, and she might wind up with a crush on him because they’re spending so much time together. I don’t want that, because I actually want Bode to stay with Chloe and be in a long-term relationship that actually lasts.

In five seasons of Fire Country, Bode really hasn’t stayed in a very serious and long-term relationship. I think it’s time for him to do that, I think Chloe is that person for him, and I don’t want CJ to get involved. Plus, I don’t want Bode and CJ’s friendship to be ruined. What they’re building platonically also feels special, and her getting in the romantic mix would change everything.

So, Fire Country, I’m begging, please let Bode and CJ just stay friends!

Now, to see how their friendship progresses, you can catch new episodes of Fire Country on CBS every Friday at 9 p.m. ET.
